units.slavonic_incipit: α) Чинъ Вечерни въ день Недѣли
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: чин вечерни в ден недели пасхи с
units.slavonic_diplomatic: α) Чинъ Вечерни въ день Недѣли Пасхи съ Евангеліемъ. — Къ сей Вечерни Іерей облекается въ вси священническія одежды, и понеже въ цѣлую свѣтлую седмицу царскія двери отворенны суть, кадитъ, и приходитъ къ св. Престолу, гдѣ съ кадилницею знаменуетъ крестовидно и возглашаетъ глаголя: „Благословенъ Богъ нашъ“ и пр., по семъ Іерей велегласно поетъ: „Христосъ воскресе“ и пр. разъ, а ликъ дваразъ. И абіе Іерей поетъ слѣдующіи стихи: „Да воскреснетъ Богъ“ и пр., „Яко исчезаетъ дымъ“ и прочіи, а ликъ по каждомъ стихѣ поетъ: „Христосъ воскресе“, при концѣ Іерей поетъ „Христосъ воскресе“ разъ, а ликъ дваразъ. Тогда Іерей глаголетъ ектенію: „Миромъ Господу помолимся“. И абіе стихиры на „Господи воззвахъ“ на 6. На „Слава и Нынѣ“ бываетъ входъ съ Евангеліемъ. На „Премудрость прости“, „Свѣте тихій“. „Вонмимъ, миръ всѣмъ, премудрость вонмимъ“ и абіе великій прокименъ. По прокименѣ „О еже сподобитися намъ“ и проч. „Миръ всѣмъ“ и проч. „Премудрость прости оуслышимъ св. Евангеліа“ и пр. (отъ Іоанна 65. „Сущу поздѣ въ день той“ и пр.). Евангеліе изъ царскихъ дверей читается, и по немъ слѣдуетъ св. Проповѣдь. По семъ ектенія: „Рцемъ вси“ и пр. „Сподоби Господи“ и пр. Ектенія: „Исполнимъ вечернія“ и пр. units.slavonic_incipit: Христе Спасе“ и пр., Іерей же
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: христе спасе и пр иерей же абие взем
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Христе Спасе“ и пр., Іерей же абіе вземъ евангеліе и крестъ, выходитъ на амвонъ и поетъ: „Да воскреснетъ Богъ“ и прочіи стихи. На сіе ликъ по каждомъ стихѣ поетъ стихиры Пасцѣ: „Пасха священная“ и проч., окончитъ же съ „Христосъ воскресе“ трижды. Подъ пѣніемъ людіе цѣлуютъ крестъ, евангеліе и образъ воскресшаго Христа. Такожде тогда бываетъ и мированіе и раздается благословенный хлѣбъ, или такъ названный антидоръ. По томъ бываетъ отпустъ великій, сирѣчь: „Премудрость“, „Благослови“ и пр. „Христосъ воскресый изъ мертвыхъ смертію смерть поправый и сущымъ въ гробѣ животъ даровавый истинный Богъ нашъ“ и пр. какъ въ Молитвословѣ стр. 478. По отпустѣ Іерей обращся къ людемъ съ крестомъ глаголетъ 3-жды: „Христосъ воскресе“, а людіе отвѣчаютъ: „Воистинну воскресе“. Благословеніе. И такъ творитъ Вечерню черезъ цѣлую свѣтлую седмицу. Въ Свѣтлой Седмицѣ всякое благословеніе съ Крестомъ бываетъ.
units.english_cohort_translation: O Christ Savior,” etc.; and the Priest immediately, having taken the Gospel and the Cross, comes forth onto the ambo and sings: “Let God arise” and the other verses. Unto this the choir after each verse sings the Paschal stichera: “A sacred Pascha,” etc., and concludes with “Christ is risen” thrice. During the singing the people kiss the Cross, the Gospel, and the icon of the risen Christ. Likewise at that time the myrovania takes place and the blessed bread, or so-called antidoron, is distributed. After that the great dismissal takes place, that is to say: “Wisdom,” “Bless,” etc., “Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and unto those in the tombs bestowing life, our true God,” etc., as in the Molitvoslov, p. 478. After the dismissal the Priest, having turned unto the people with the Cross, says thrice: “Christ is risen!” and the people answer: “Truly He is risen!” Blessing. And thus he celebrates Vespers throughout the entire Bright Week. In Bright Week every blessing takes place with the Cross.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: β) Чинъ Вечерни въ свѣтлой седмицѣ, если случится въ нѣкій день Святый полуелейный. — Іерей одѣявъ вси одежды и покадивъ церковь, предъ св. Трапезою начинаетъ отъ: „Благословенъ Богъ нашъ“. По семъ: „Христосъ воскресе“ 3-жды съ стихами. На конецъ Іерей поетъ: „Христосъ воскресе“ разъ, ликъ же дваразъ. И абіе ектенія мирная. (Кадизмы нѣтъ въ свѣтлой седмицѣ.) На „Господи воззвахъ“ стихиры 6, и то 3 Воскресенію, а 3 Святому. Слава: Святаго, И нынѣ: Богородиченъ догматъ, т. е. первый гласа. Входъ съ кадиломъ. Прокименъ дню. Чтенія Святаго. На стиховнѣхъ стихира одна воскресна, прочіи же стихиры Пасцѣ. (Цѣлованіе креста.) Слава: Святаго, И нынѣ: „Воскресенія день“ и пр. „Христосъ воскресе“ 3-жды. И абіе Слава: Тропарь Святому, И нынѣ: Богородиченъ по гласу Святаго. Отпустъ Пасхи съ Крестомъ. Благословеніе съ Крестомъ черезъ цѣлую Седмицу.
units.english_cohort_translation: (β) Order of Vespers in Bright Week, if on a certain day a polyeleos Saint should occur. — The Priest, having put on all the vestments and censed the church, before the Holy Table begins from: “Blessed is our God.” After this: “Christ is risen” thrice with the verses. At the end the Priest sings: “Christ is risen” once, and the choir twice. And immediately the litany of peace. (There is no kathisma in Bright Week.) At “Lord, I have cried,” 6 stichera, namely 3 of the Resurrection, and 3 unto the Saint. “Glory,” of the Saint; “Now and,” Theotokion-dogmaticon, that is, the first of the tone. Entrance with the censer. Prokimenon of the day. Readings of the Saint. At the aposticha, one sticheron of the Resurrection, and the rest the stichera of Pascha. (Veneration of the Cross.) “Glory,” of the Saint; “Now and,” “The Day of Resurrection,” etc., “Christ is risen” thrice. And immediately “Glory,” Troparion unto the Saint; “Now and,” Theotokion according to the tone of the Saint. Paschal dismissal with the Cross. Blessing with the Cross throughout the entire week.

units.slavonic_incipit: Примѣчаніе. Что касается вечерней отъ Недѣли
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: примечание что касается вечерней от недели фоминой до
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Примѣчаніе. Что касается вечерней отъ Недѣли Ѳоминой до Вознесенія, о сихъ слѣдующія потребно замѣтити: α) Вечерня недѣльная поемая въ Субботу вечеръ, чинится сице: По „Благословенъ Богъ нашъ“ Іерей поетъ „Христосъ воскресе“ разъ, а пѣвецъ два разъ. (Стихи не поются.) И абіе Трисвятое.*) Отче нашъ съ возгласомъ. Господи пом. 12. Прійдите покл. 3. Псаломъ предначинательный: „Благослови душе моя“. Ектенія мирная. Кадизма. На „Господи воззвахъ“ стихиры 10.**) Входъ великій.
units.english_cohort_translation: Note. Concerning Vespers from Thomas Sunday until Ascension, it is necessary to note the following regarding these: (α) Sunday Vespers, sung on Saturday evening, is celebrated thus: After “Blessed is our God” the Priest sings “Christ is risen” once, and the cantor twice. (The verses are not sung.) And immediately the Trisagion.[^98] “Our Father” with the Exclamation. “Lord, have mercy” (12 times). “Come, let us worship” (thrice). The Introductory Psalm: “Bless the Lord, O my soul.” Litany of peace. Kathisma. At “Lord, I have cried,” 10 stichera.[^99] Great entrance.

units.slavonic_incipit: Єктеніи 2. На стиховнѣхъ одна стихира
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: ектении 2 на стиховнех одна стихира воскресна по
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Єктеніи 2. На стиховнѣхъ одна стихира воскресна по ряду изъ Тріоди цвѣтной, и абіе поются стихиры Пасцѣ (изнявше Недѣлю Ѳомину) „Да воскреснетъ Богъ“ и пр. „Пасха священная“ и пр. Слава: Святаго, если есть; И нынѣ: „Воскресенія день“, и одинъ разъ: „Христосъ воскресе“ и такъ „Нынѣ отпущаеши“. (Когда поются стихиры Пасцѣ, Іерей растворяетъ царскія двери, выходитъ на амвонъ и даетъ людямъ крестъ цѣловати.) По „Нынѣ отпущаеши“ поются тропари и абіе отпустъ Пасхи съ Крестомъ. — β) О повседневной Вечерни то потребно замѣтити, что сей Вечерни начало есть такое, какъ и недѣльной. Она отправляется порядочно. По ектеніи кадизма дню, Стихиры на „Господи воззвахъ“ 6, и то и Святому. Входа нѣтъ. Стихиры на стиховнѣхъ воскресны изъ Тріоди Цвѣтной (а не Пасцѣ.) Слава: Святому, И нынѣ: Богородиченъ. По „Нынѣ отпущаеши“ вся порядочно. (Стихиры Пасцѣ на повседневной Вечерни лишь въ Вторникъ вечеръ на отданіе праздника Пасхи берутся.) Отпустъ безъ Креста, т. е. Премудрость. „Воскресый изъ мертвыхъ“ и пр.
units.english_cohort_translation: 2 litanies. At the aposticha, one sticheron of the Resurrection in order from the Flowery Triodion, and immediately the stichera of Pascha are sung (except on Thomas Sunday): “Let God arise,” etc., “A sacred Pascha,” etc. “Glory,” of the Saint, if there be one; “Now and,” “The Day of Resurrection,” and once: “Christ is risen”; and thus “Now Thou lettest depart.” (When the stichera of Pascha are sung, the Priest opens the royal doors, comes forth onto the ambo, and gives the Cross unto the people to kiss.) After “Now Thou lettest depart” the troparia are sung and immediately the dismissal of Pascha with the Cross. — (β) Concerning daily Vespers, it is necessary to note that the beginning of this Vespers is the same as that of Sunday Vespers. It is celebrated in order. After the litany, the kathisma of the day; the stichera at “Lord, I have cried” on 6, and that also unto the Saint. There is no entrance. The stichera at the aposticha are of the Resurrection from the Flowery Triodion (and not of Pascha). “Glory,” unto the Saint; “Now and,” Theotokion. After “Now Thou lettest depart,” all in order. (The stichera of Pascha at daily Vespers are taken only on Tuesday evening at the Apodosis of the Feast of Pascha.) The dismissal is without the Cross, that is to say: “Wisdom”; “He Who rose from the dead,” etc.

units.slavonic_incipit: Вечерня сія въ Недѣлю Сош. св.
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: вечерня сия в неделю сош св духа абие
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Вечерня сія въ Недѣлю Сош. св. Духа абіе отправляется по св. Литургіи и то совокупно съ колѣнопреклонными молитвами ради призыванія св. Духа. Чинъ сей Вечерни есть слѣдующій. По „Буди имя Господне“ Іерей вшедъ въ св. олтарь, начинаетъ: „Благословенъ Богъ нашъ“ и пр. и глаголетъ „Царю небесный“, Трисвятое и прочее начала обычайнаго и Ѱаломъ: „Благослови душе моя“ и проч. По „Аллилуя 3. Слава Тебѣ Боже“ Іерей поетъ ектенію мирную, къ которой по моленіи: „О предстоящихъ людехъ“ прилагаетъ и особенную ектенію „О призываніи помощи св. Духа“ находящуюся въ Служебникѣ, которою съ колѣнопреклоненіемъ глаголетъ. По возгласѣ: „Яко подобаетъ“, ликъ поетъ: „Господи воззвахъ“ и стихиры. (Кадизмы нѣтъ.) Слава и Нынѣ. Входъ съ кадилницею. Прокименъ великій: „Кто Богъ велій“ и проч. По прокименѣ Іерей взыйдетъ на амвонъ и возглашаетъ: „Паки и паки колѣна приклонше Господу помолимся“, и приклонивъ колѣна, чтетъ молитву І-ую: „Пречисте, нескверне“ и пр. По семъ вставше, глаголетъ ектенію малую: „Заступи, спаси“ и проч. далѣе ектенію: „Рцемъ вси“. — По ектеніи возглашаетъ: „Паки и паки преклонше колѣна“ и проч. и чтетъ ІІ-ую молитву:
units.english_cohort_translation: Order of Vespers on the Descent of the Holy Spirit This Vespers on Sunday of the Descent of the Holy Spirit is celebrated immediately after the Divine Liturgy, and that together with the kneeling prayers for the invocation of the Holy Spirit. The order of this Vespers is as follows: After “Blessed be the name of the Lord” the Priest, having entered into the holy altar, begins: “Blessed is our God,” etc., and says “Heavenly King,” the Trisagion, and the rest of the ordinary beginning, and the Psalm: “Bless the Lord, O my soul,” etc. After “Alleluia” (thrice), “Glory to Thee, O God,” the Priest chants the litany of peace, unto which after the petition: “For the people here present” he appends also the special litany “For the invocation of the help of the Holy Spirit” found in the *Sluzhebnik*, which he recites with kneeling. After the exclamation: “For unto Thee is due,” the choir sings: “Lord, I have cried” and the stichera. (There is no kathisma.) “Glory,” and “Now and.” Entrance with the censer. Great Prokimenon: “Who is a God as great as our God?” etc. After the prokimenon the Priest ascends onto the ambo and proclaims: “Again and again, having bowed our knees, let us pray unto the Lord,” and having bowed his knees, recites the 1st prayer: “O undefiled, unblemished,” etc. After this, having arisen, he says the small litany: “Help us, save us,” etc., and then the litany: “Let us all say.” — After the litany he proclaims: “Again and again, having bowed our knees,” etc., and recites the 2nd prayer:

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: господи иисусе христе и пр по сей молитве
units.slavonic_diplomatic: „Господи, Іисусе Христе“ и пр. По сей молитвѣ вновь поетъ ектенію малую: „Заступи, спаси“ и пр., и абіе ликъ читаетъ: „Сподоби Господи“. По семъ Іерей опять глаголетъ: „Паки и паки колѣна преклонше“ и пр. и чтетъ ІІІ-ью молитву: „Приснотекущій, животворный“ и пр. По семъ: „Заступи, спаси“ и проч. и Ектенія: „Исполнимъ вечернія“ и пр. units.slavonic_incipit: Въ навечеріе Рождества Іисуса Христа порядочно
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: в навечерие рождества иисуса христа порядочно кончатся оутром
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Въ навечеріе Рождества Іисуса Христа порядочно кончатся оутромъ часы царскіи совокупно съ Вечернею и Литургіею св. Василія Великаго. Но если Навечеріе впадетъ на Субботу или на Недѣлю, то отправа подѣлится и то такъ: что часы царскіи предварительно отправляются въ Пятокъ, Вечерня отправляется въ самое Навечеріе (т. е. въ Субботу или въ Недѣлю) вечеромъ 3-го часа съ парамеями вечерными, съ тропарями и съ Апостоломъ и Евангеліемъ Навечерія, Литургія же св. Василія отправляется въ самый день Рождества Христоваго. — О сей великой Вечерни то примѣтимъ, что она имѣетъ начало обычайное. Стихиры на „Господи воззвахъ“ Рождества на 8. Входъ съ кадиломъ и съ Евангеліемъ. По „Свѣте тихій“ Іерей возглашаетъ „Вонмимъ, миръ всѣмъ, премудрость вонмимъ“ и поется прокименъ дню, послѣ котораго бываютъ чтенія 8 съ тропарями. Сіи тропари на 3-ой и по 6-ой пареміи суть вмѣщенны. По скончаніи 8-го чтенія ект. малая и абіе „Вонмимъ, миръ всѣмъ, премудрость вонмимъ“ и берется прокименъ Апостола: „Господь рече ко мнѣ“. — Читается Апостолъ зач. 303. Аллилуя и Еванг. отъ Мат. зач. 53. Потомъ „Рцемъ вси“, „Сподоби Господи“ и „Исполнимъ вечернія молитвы“ и абіе великій отпустъ. — (Стихиры на стиховнѣхъ не суть.)

units.slavonic_incipit: Примѣчаніе. Семъ сходно подѣлится и отправа
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: примечание сем сходно поделится и отправа навечерия богоявления
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Примѣчаніе. Семъ сходно подѣлится и отправа Навечерія Богоявленія, если оно случится въ Субботу или Недѣлю. Тѣй кромѣ того еще и то потребно примѣтити, что Вечерня сія въ семъ случаѣ не токмо сей подобна есть, но она еще въ такомъ случаю совокупляется и съ водосвятіемъ. — Сирѣчь
units.english_cohort_translation:
On the Paramony of the Nativity of Jesus Christ, the Royal Hours conclude in order in the morning together with Vespers and the Divine Liturgy of St. Basil the Great. But if the Paramony should fall on a Saturday or on a Sunday, the celebration is divided, and that thus: the Royal Hours are celebrated beforehand on Friday; Vespers is celebrated on the Paramony itself (that is, on Saturday or on Sunday) in the evening at the 3rd hour with the evening paremias, with the troparia, and with the Epistle and Gospel of the Paramony; while the Divine Liturgy of St. Basil is celebrated on the very day of the Nativity of Christ. — Concerning this Great Vespers we note that it hath the ordinary beginning. Stichera at “Lord, I have cried” of the Nativity on 8. Entrance with the censer and with the Gospel. After “Gladsome Light” the Priest proclaims: “Let us attend! Peace be to all! Wisdom, let us attend!” and the prokimenon of the day is sung, after which there are 8 readings with troparia. These troparia are inserted at the 3rd and after the 6th paremia. At the conclusion of the 8th reading, the small litany, and immediately: “Let us attend! Peace be to all! Wisdom, let us attend!” and the prokimenon of the Epistle is taken: “The Lord said unto Me” [Ps. 2:7]. — The Epistle is read, pericope 303 [Gal. 3:15–22]. Alleluia and the Gospel from Matthew, pericope 53. Then “Let us all say,” “Vouchsafe, O Lord,” and “Let us complete our evening prayer,” and immediately the great dismissal. — (There are no stichera at the aposticha.)
Note. In like manner the celebration of the Paramony of Theophany is divided, if it should occur on a Saturday or Sunday. Тѣй кромѣ того еще и то потребно примѣтити, что Вечерня сія въ семъ случаѣ не токмо сей подобна есть, но она еще въ такомъ случаю совокупляется и съ водосвятіемъ. — Сирѣчь
units.english_text:
On the Paramony of the Nativity of Jesus Christ, the Royal Hours conclude in order in the morning together with Vespers and the Divine Liturgy of St. Basil the Great. But if the Paramony should fall on a Saturday or on a Sunday, the celebration is divided, and that thus: the Royal Hours are celebrated beforehand on Friday; Vespers is celebrated on the Paramony itself (that is, on Saturday or on Sunday) in the evening at the 3rd hour with the evening paremias, with the troparia, and with the Epistle and Gospel of the Paramony; while the Divine Liturgy of St. Basil is celebrated on the very day of the Nativity of Christ. — Concerning this Great Vespers we note that it hath the ordinary beginning. Stichera at “Lord, I have cried” of the Nativity on 8. Entrance with the censer and with the Gospel. After “Gladsome Light” the Priest proclaims: “Let us attend! Peace be to all! Wisdom, let us attend!” and the prokimenon of the day is sung, after which there are 8 readings with troparia. These troparia are inserted at the 3rd and after the 6th paremia. At the conclusion of the 8th reading, the small litany, and immediately: “Let us attend! Peace be to all! Wisdom, let us attend!” and the prokimenon of the Epistle is taken: “The Lord said unto Me” [Ps. 2:7]. — The Epistle is read, pericope 303 [Gal. 3:15–22]. Alleluia and the Gospel from Matthew, pericope 53. Then “Let us all say,” “Vouchsafe, O Lord,” and “Let us complete our evening prayer,” and immediately the great dismissal. — (There are no stichera at the aposticha.)
Note. In like manner the celebration of the Paramony of Theophany is divided, if it should occur on a Saturday or Sunday. There, in addition, it is also necessary to note that this Vespers in this case is not only similar to this one, but in such a case it is also combined with the blessing of water. — That is to say, after the readings, after the Epistle and Gospel and after both litanies, the Priest comes forth into the midst of the church, where water is prepared, and the choir begins to sing: “The voice of the Lord is upon the waters,” and the blessing of water is celebrated, concerning which mention will be made in Article III.

units.slavonic_incipit: Малое Повечеріе оу насъ публично въ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: малое повечерие оу нас публично в церкви лиш
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Малое Повечеріе оу насъ публично въ церкви лишь въ страстную Середу, Пятокъ и Субботу и на Сошествіе св. Духа отправляется, приватно же дома черезъ цѣлый годъ, еще и въ Великомъ Постѣ въ Субботу и въ Недѣлю (т. е. на Недѣлю и на Понедѣлокъ.) Великое же отправляется публично: α) въ Вторникъ и въ Четверъ (т. е. на Середу и на Пятокъ) сыропустной седмицы. β) Въ Понедѣлокъ, Вторникъ, Середу (съ изятіемъ Середы 5-ой седмицы), Четверъ и Пятокъ (съ изятіемъ Пятка 5-ой седмицы) всѣхъ седмицъ великаго Поста. γ) Въ Понедѣлокъ и Вторникъ страстной седмицы. δ) Въ Навечеріе Рождества Христова и Богоявленія. ε) Въ Навечеріе Благовѣщенія, если той праздникъ случится въ Вторникъ, Середу, Четверъ, Пятокъ и Субботу першихъ 6 седмицъ Великаго Поста, алько если случится въ Вторникъ, Середу и Четверъ страстной седмицы.
units.english_cohort_translation: Small Compline among us is celebrated publicly in church only on Holy Wednesday, Friday, and Saturday, and on the Descent of the Holy Spirit; but privately at home throughout the entire year, even in the Great Fast on Saturday and on Sunday (that is, for Sunday and for Monday). Great Compline, however, is celebrated publicly: (α) on Tuesday and on Thursday (that is, for Wednesday and for Friday) of Cheesefare Week; (β) on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday (with the exception of Wednesday of the 5th week), Thursday, and Friday (with the exception of Friday of the 5th week) of all weeks of the Great Fast; (γ) on Monday and Tuesday of Passion Week; (δ) on the Paramony of the Nativity of Christ and of Theophany; (ε) on the Paramony of the Annunciation, if that feast should occur on Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, or Saturday of the first 6 weeks of the Great Fast, or if it should occur on Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday of Passion Week.

units.slavonic_incipit: И абіе: Царю небесный. Трисвятое. Отче
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: и абие царю небесный трисвятое отче наш с
units.slavonic_diplomatic: И абіе: Царю небесный. Трисвятое. Отче нашъ съ Возгласомъ. Госп. пом. 12. Прійдите покл. 3. По семъ Іерей входитъ въ св. олтарь, а ликъ читаетъ: псалмы, и то 50-ый (Помилуй мя Боже) 69., и 142-ый (Господи оуслыши молитву мою), по псалмахъ же читаетъ: Слава въ вышнихъ Богъ. Вѣрую. По семъ поется канонъ дневный въ честь Пресв. Богородицы изъ Октоиха.*) (Катавасіа по каждой пѣсни не поется.) По ІІІ-ой пѣсни не поется ектенія, но глаголется: Господи пом. 3. Слава и Нынѣ и Сѣдаленъ. По VI-ой пѣсни такожде: Господи пом. 3. Слава и Нынѣ: Кондакъ и Ікосъ. По окончаніи ІХ-ой пѣсни оба лики совокупно поютъ: „Достойно“**) По семъ: Трисвятое. Отче нашъ съ Возгласомъ. Въ Субботу Ѵпакой гласа, если же праздникъ или нарочитый Святый, Кондакъ его; а если день простый, тропарь храму, дню и настоящій: „Боже Отецъ нашихъ“ и пр. (Молитвосл. стр. 271.) Господи пом. 40. Подъ симъ Іерей выходитъ и чтетъ предъ царскими враты молитву „Иже на всякое“ и пр. Ликъ Господи пом. 3. Слава и Нынѣ. Честнѣйшую и пр. Именемъ Господнимъ благослови Отче. И Іерей возглашаетъ: „Боже оущедри ны“ и пр. По „Аминь“ же возглашаетъ молитву: „Нескверная, неблазная“ и проч. и приключаетъ молитву: „И даждь намъ“ и проч. съ „Преславная“ и „Оупованіе намъ“ и пр. По семъ поются тропари: „Помилуй насъ Господи помилуй насъ“ и пр. Слава: „Господи помилуй насъ“ и пр. И нынѣ: „Милосердія двери“ и пр. По сихъ ектенія: „Помилуй насъ Боже“ и пр. „Еще молимся, о еже сохранитися граду сему...“ и по возгласѣ: „Оуслыши ны Боже Спасителю...“ Отпустъ найменшій ѿ „Слава Тебѣ Христе Боже“. По семъ поминанія.***) Если же оутріе будетъ недѣля, праздникъ, или нарочитый Святый, тогда Іерей по „О оумноженіи плодовъ земныхъ“ не поминаетъ оусопшихъ, лишь живыхъ, и прото абіе будетъ „Молитвами свят. Отецъ“ и проч. и такъ бываетъ благословеніе.

units.slavonic_incipit: Часть І-ая. Іерей въ епитрахилѣ творитъ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: част и ая иерей в епитрахиле творит начало обычное
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Часть І-ая. Іерей въ епитрахилѣ творитъ начало обычное, глаголя: „Благословенъ Богъ нашъ“ и пр. Ликъ: „Аминь“. И абіе: Царю небесный. Трисвятое. Отче нашъ съ возгласомъ. Господи пом. 12. Слава и Нынѣ. Прійдите покл. 3. Подъ симъ Іерей входитъ въ св. олтарь, пѣвецъ же начнетъ читати псалмы: 4., 6., 12. Слава и Нынѣ. Аллилуя 3. Господи пом. 3. Слава и Нынѣ. Опять псалмы: 24., 30., 90. Слава и Нынѣ. Аллилуя 3. Господи пом. 3. По псалмахъ Іерей выходитъ и велегласитъ пѣніе: „Съ нами Богъ разумѣйте языцы и покаряйтеся, яко съ нами Богъ“, ликъ тожде 2-жды. По семъ Іерей поетъ стихи, ликъ же повторяетъ на единокаждый стихъ „Съ нами Богъ“. По скончаніи сего пѣнія Іерей входитъ, а пѣвецъ читаетъ: „День прешедъ“ и проч. Безплотное. Вѣрую. Пресвятая. Трисвятое. Отче нашъ съ возгласомъ, и абіе поются тропари. По тропаряхъ ликъ: Господи пом. 40. (и Іерей выходитъ). Слава и Нынѣ. Честнѣйшую. Именемъ Господнимъ благослови Отче. И Іерей возглашаетъ: „Молитвами св. Отецъ“ и пр., и молитвою: „Господи, Господи“ и пр. окончитъ І-ую часть, вшедъ въ олтарь.
units.english_cohort_translation: Part I. The Priest in epitrachelion makes the ordinary beginning, saying: “Blessed is our God,” etc. The choir: “Amen.” And immediately: “Heavenly King.” The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. “Lord, have mercy” (12 times). “Glory,” and “Now and.” “Come, let us worship” (thrice). During this the Priest enters into the holy altar, and the cantor begins to read the Psalms: 4, 6, 12. “Glory,” and “Now and.” “Alleluia” (thrice). “Lord, have mercy” (thrice). “Glory,” and “Now and.” Again the Psalms: 24, 30, 90. “Glory,” and “Now and.” “Alleluia” (thrice). “Lord, have mercy” (thrice). After the Psalms the Priest comes forth and loudly chants the hymn: “God is with us, understand, all ye nations, and submit yourselves, for God is with us”; the choir chants the same twice. After this the Priest chants the verses, and the choir repeats after each verse: “God is with us.” At the conclusion of this singing the Priest enters, and the cantor reads: “The day being past,” etc. “The bodiless.” The Creed. “Most Holy.” The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation, and immediately the troparia are sung. After the troparia the choir: “Lord, have mercy” (40 times) (and the Priest comes forth). “Glory,” and “Now and.” “More honorable.” “In the name of the Lord bless, Father.” And the Priest proclaims: “Through the prayers of our holy Fathers,” etc., and with the prayer: “O Lord, Lord,” etc., concludes the 1st part, having entered into the altar.

По семъ слѣдуетъ тропарь: „Господи силъ“ и пр. съ псал. 150. „Хвалите Бога въ святыхъ его“ который такъ спѣвается, что до каждаго стиха того псалма припѣвается: „Господи силъ“, на Слава же спѣвается: „Господи аще не быхомъ“ и пр., а на И нынѣ: „Многая множества“ и пр. units.english_cohort_translation: Part III. This part begins with the invitation: “Come, let us worship” (thrice); the Psalms: the 69th (“O God, come to my assistance” [Ps. 69]) and the 142nd (“O Lord, hear my prayer” [Ps. 142]). After this: “Glory to God in the highest” is only read. A canon, sometimes even two.[^103] After the canon there is sung the hymn: “It is truly right.” The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. After this follows the troparion: “O Lord of hosts,” etc., with Psalm 150: “Praise God in His saints” [Ps. 150:1], which is sung in such a manner that unto each verse of that Psalm there is appended as a refrain: “O Lord of hosts”; and at “Glory” there is sung: “O Lord, if we had not Thy saints,” etc., and at “Now and”: “A multitude of transgressions,” etc. After this: “O Most Holy Theotokos.” “All my hope.” After this follows “Lord, have mercy” (40 times). And the Priest comes forth and recites the prayer: “Thou Who at all times,” etc., and the choir:

units.english_cohort_translation: Order of Small Compline without a Canon The beginning of this Compline is ordinary, with the Psalms and with “I believe in one God,” etc. — After the Creed there is no canon, but immediately “It is truly right,” and immediately the Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. After this the troparion of the temple, of the day, and “O God of our Fathers.” After the troparia: “Lord, have mercy” (40 times), “Thou Who at all times.” “Lord, have mercy” (thrice), “More honorable,” “In the name of the Lord bless, Father.” And the Priest proclaims: “God be merciful unto us,” etc. After this: “O undefiled,” and “And grant unto us,” “O most glorious,” “Our hope.” Troparia: “Have mercy on us, O Lord,” etc. Litany: “Have mercy on us, O God,” etc. Dismissal. Commemorations.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: чин повечерия малаго с поклонами повечерие
units.slavonic_diplomatic: α) Чинъ Повечерія малаго съ поклонами. — Повечеріе сіе Іерей долженъ въ домѣ своемъ читати по недѣлямъ вел. Поста. Оно есть Повечеріе Понедѣлька.**) Отправляется же сице: Начало обычайное. „Благословенъ Богъ нашъ“ и пр. Прій- *) Зри Пелешъ, Богословіе Пастырское, стр. 603.
units.english_cohort_translation:
Order of Complines in the Holy Great Fast (α) Order of Small Compline with Prostrations. — This Compline the Priest must read in his own house on Sundays of the Great Fast. It is the Compline of Monday.[^105] It is celebrated thus: Ordinary beginning: “Blessed is our God,” etc. Come, let us worship (thrice). The Psalms: 50, 69, and 142. After this: “Glory to God in the highest,” the Creed. The Theotokion canon. After the canon: “It is truly right.” The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. And immediately: the troparia of the temple, of the day, and the present one: “O God of our Fathers.”[^106] After the troparia the choir says: “Lord, have mercy” (40 times); the Priest, having come forth, says the prayer: “Thou Who at all times.” The choir: “Lord, have mercy” (thrice), “Glory,” and “Now and,” “More honorable,” “In the name of the Lord bless, Father.” The Priest proclaims: “God be merciful unto us,” etc., and makes 3 great prostrations with the prayer of St. Ephrem (“O Lord and Master of my life”). After this, the Trisagion (thrice), “O Most Holy Trinity,” “Our Father” with the exclamation. “Lord, have mercy” (12 times). The prayer: “O undefiled,” etc., “And grant unto us,” “O most glorious,” “Our hope,” etc. The smallest dismissal from “Glory to Thee, O Christ God, our hope, glory to Thee.” The commemorations, and thus the blessing. (The troparia: “Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us,” etc., and the litany: “Have mercy on us, O God,” are omitted.)
(β) Order of Great Compline in the First Week of the Holy Great Fast. — Part I. The Priest in epitrachelion begins, saying: “Blessed is our God,” unto which the choir: “Amen.” And immediately: “Heavenly King.” The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. “Lord, have mercy” (12 times). “Glory,” and “Now and.” “Come, let us worship” (thrice). Then the Priest enters into the holy altar, and the cantor reads the 69th Psalm (“O God, come to my assistance” [Ps. 69]). After the Psalm, the Great Canon of St. Andrew of Crete.[^107] After the canon “It is truly right” is not sung, but instead of it the 9th ode is repeated, and one prostration even unto the ground is made. After this the Psalms: 4, 6, 12. “Glory,” and “Now and.” “Alleluia” (thrice). “Lord, have mercy” (thrice). “Glory,” and “Now and,” and immediately the Psalms: 24, 30, 90. “Glory,” and “Now and.” “Alleluia” (thrice). “Lord, have mercy” (thrice). And the Priest, having come forth, chants the hymn: “God is with us,” the choir twice. The Priest chants the verses, the cantor appends after each verse: “God is with us.” After this hymn the Priest enters into the holy altar, and the cantor reads: “The day being past,” etc., “The bodiless nature,” etc., “Most Holy Virgin.” The Creed. “O Most Holy Lady, pray to God for us sinners” — twice; while the 1st choir recites, the other makes a prostration, — and while the other choir arises and answers, the 1st choir makes a prostration. Likewise also at the other verses.[^108] After these petitions, the Trisagion, “Our Father” with the exclamation. After this on Monday and Wednesday the troparia: “Enlighten mine eyes,”

units.slavonic_incipit: въ Вторникъ же и Четверъ: „Невидимыхъ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: в вторник же и четвер невидимых враг моих
units.slavonic_diplomatic: въ Вторникъ же и Четверъ: „Невидимыхъ врагъ моихъ“.*) Послѣ сихъ тропарей: Господи пом. 40. Слава и Нынѣ. Честнѣйшую и пр. Именемъ Господнимъ благослови Отче. И Іерей предъ царскими враты возглашаетъ: „Молитвами св. Отецъ“ и пр., и чтетъ молитву: „Господи, Господи избавлея насъ“ и пр. и симъ кончится І. часть сего Повечерія. — ІІ-ая часть начинается съ Прійдите поклонимся 3. По семъ псалмы: 50., 101. („Господи оуслыши молитву мою“.) По сихъ псалмахъ Іерей чтетъ молитву: „Господи Вседержителю“ и проч. По семъ: Трисвятое. Отче нашъ съ возгласомъ. И абіе поемъ тропари: „Помилуй насъ Господи“ и пр. Господи пом. 40. Слава и Нынѣ. Честнѣйшую. Именемъ Господнимъ благослови Отче. И Іерей возглашаетъ: „Господи Іисусе Христе Боже нашъ помилуй насъ“ и чтетъ молитву: „Владыко Боже Отче“ и пр., которою разомъ и окончитъ ІІ-ую часть. ІІІ-ая часть начинается съ Прійдите покл. 3. По семъ понеже псаломъ 69. „Боже въ помощь мою“ оставляется, сей часъ берется псаломъ 142-ый („Господи оуслыши молитву мою“.) По псалмѣ: „Слава въ вышнихъ Богъ“. Далѣе: Трисвятое. Отче нашъ съ возгласомъ. По семъ поется велегласно и косно: „Господи силъ съ нами“ съ стихами на „Хвалите“-хъ. Слава: „Господи аще не быхомъ“, И нынѣ: „Многая множества“. Далѣе: „Всесвятая Богородице“. „Все оупованіе“. Господи пом. 40. „Иже на всякое“. Господи пом. 3. Слава и Нынѣ. Честнѣйшую. Именемъ Господнимъ благослови Отче. И Іерей возглашаетъ: „Боже оущедри ны“ и пр. и чинитъ 3 поклоны съ молитвою св. Ефрема. По поклонахъ Трисвятое. Отче нашъ съ возгласомъ. Господи пом. 12. и молитвы (колѣна приклонше): „Нескверная“ и „И даждь намъ“, „Преславная“, „Оупованіе намъ“. По семъ отпустъ найменьшій отъ: „Слава Тебѣ Христе Боже оупованіе наше слава Тебѣ“. Ликъ: Слава и Нынѣ. Господи пом. 3. Благослови Іерей же вмѣсто отпуста глаголетъ молитву литійную: „Владыко многомилостиве“. По скончанію сей молитвы слѣдуютъ сей часъ поминанія и благословеніе.
units.english_cohort_translation: and on Tuesday and Thursday: “Mine unseen enemies.”[^109] After these troparia: “Lord, have mercy” (40 times), “Glory,” and “Now and,” “More honorable,” etc., “In the name of the Lord bless, Father.” And the Priest before the royal doors proclaims: “Through the prayers of our holy Fathers,” etc., and recites the prayer: “O Lord, Lord, Who deliverest us,” etc., and herewith the 1st part of this Compline is concluded. — Part II begins with “Come, let us worship” (thrice). After this the Psalms: 50, 101 (“O Lord, hear my prayer” [Ps. 101]). After these Psalms the Priest recites the prayer: “O Lord Almighty,” etc. After this: The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. And immediately we sing the troparia: “Have mercy on us, O Lord,” etc. “Lord, have mercy” (40 times). “Glory,” and “Now and.” “More honorable.” “In the name of the Lord bless, Father.” And the Priest proclaims: “O Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us,” and recites the prayer: “O Master, God the Father,” etc., with which at once he also concludes the 2nd part. Part III begins with “Come, let us worship” (thrice). After this, since Psalm 69, “O God, come to my assistance,” is omitted, immediately the 142nd Psalm is taken (“O Lord, hear my prayer” [Ps. 142]). units.slavonic_diplomatic: γ) Чинъ Повечерія великаго въ прочія седмицы Вел. Поста. — Сіе Повечеріе есть подобно прежде сказанномъ, лишь въ томъ разниствуетъ отъ него, что канонъ на концѣ глаголется. Отправляется же сице: Часть І. „Благословенъ Богъ нашъ“ и прочее начала обычнаго. По Прійдите покл. 3. Ѱалмы: 4., 6., 12. Слава и Нынѣ. Ѱалмы: 24., 30. и 90-ый. Слава и *) Молитвословъ стр. 288.
units.english_cohort_translation: (γ) Order of Great Compline in the Remaining Weeks of the Great Fast. — This Compline is similar to that previously described, differing from it only in that the canon is recited at the end. It is celebrated thus: Part I. “Blessed is our God,” and the rest of the ordinary beginning. After “Come, let us worship” (thrice), the Psalms: 4, 6, 12. “Glory,” and “Now and.” The Psalms: 24, 30, and the 90th. “Glory,” and “Now and.” “Alleluia” (thrice). “Lord, have mercy” (thrice). “Glory,” and “Now and.” The singing: “God is with us.” The petitions: “The day being past, I give thanks,” etc. “Glory,” “The day being past, I glorify,” etc. “Now and,” “The day being past, I hymn,” etc. “The bodiless.” “Most Holy Virgin.” The Creed. “O Most Holy Lady.” The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation, and immediately the troparia, on Monday and Wednesday: “Enlighten mine eyes,” on Tuesday and Thursday: “Mine unseen enemies.” “Lord, have mercy” (40 times). “Glory,” and “Now and.” “More honorable.” “In the name of the Lord bless, Father.” And the Priest proclaims: “Through the prayers of our holy Fathers,” etc., and recites the prayer: “O Lord, Lord,” with which he concludes the 1st part. Part II begins with “Come, let us worship” (thrice). After this the Psalms: 50 and the 101st. The prayer of King Manasses: “O Lord Almighty,” etc. The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. Troparia: “Have mercy on us, O Lord,” etc. “Lord, have mercy” (40 times). “Glory,” and “Now and.” “More honorable.” “In the name of the Lord bless, Father.” And the Priest proclaims: “O Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us,” etc., and with the prayer: “O Master, God the Father,” etc., concludes the 2nd part.

After this the Psalms: 69 and the 142nd. “Glory to God in the highest.” The canon in honor of the Most Holy Theotokos. “It is truly right.” When the choir concludes: “It is truly right,” the Priest, having come forth before the royal doors, makes one prostration (except on Friday). After this: The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. “O Lord of hosts,”[^110] with the verses at the Praises. “Glory,” “O Lord, if we had not.” “Now and,” “A multitude of transgressions,” and the rest. “Lord, have mercy” (50 times). “Thou Who at all times.” “Lord, have mercy” (thrice). “Glory,” and “Now and.” “More honorable.” “In the name of the Lord bless, Father,” and the Priest proclaims: “God be merciful unto us,” etc., and makes the prostrations. After the prostrations, the Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. “Lord, have mercy” (12 times), and the Priest, having bowed his knees, says the prayers: “O undefiled,” “And grant unto us,” “O most glorious,” “Our hope,” and after this immediately says the smallest dismissal from “Glory to Thee, O Christ God,” etc. The choir: “Glory,” and “Now and,” “Lord, have mercy” (thrice), “Bless,” unto which the Priest says instead of the dismissal the Litiya prayer: “O most merciful Master,” etc. After the prayer, the commemorations and the blessing.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: ІІІ-ая часть начинается отъ „Прійдите покл. 3.“ По семъ Ѱалмы: 69. и 142-ый. „Слава въ вышнихъ“. Канонъ въ честь пресв. Богородицы. „Достойно“. Когда ликъ окончиваетъ: „Достойно“, Іерей изшедъ предъ царскія двери, чинитъ одинъ поклонъ (изнявше Пятокъ.) По семъ Трисвятое. Отче нашъ съ возгласомъ. „Господи силъ“*) съ стихами на „Хвалите“-хъ. Слава: „Господи аще не быхомъ“. И нынѣ: „Многая множества“ и прочая. Господи пом. 50. „Иже на всякое время“. Господи пом. 3. Слава и Нынѣ. Честнѣйшую. Именемъ Господнимъ благослови Отче“, и Іерей возглашаетъ: „Боже оущедри ны“ и проч. и чинитъ поклоны. По поклонахъ Трисвятое. Отче нашъ съ возгласомъ. Господи пом. 12. и Іерей колѣна приклонше глаголетъ молитвы: „Нескверная“, „И даждь намъ“, „Преславная“, „Оупованіе намъ“ и по семъ абіе глаголетъ отпустъ найменьшій отъ „Слава Тебѣ Христе Боже“ и пр. Ликъ Слава и Нынѣ. Господи пом. 3. Благослови, на что Іерей глаголетъ мѣсто отпуста молитву Литійную: „Владыко многомилостиве“ и пр. По молитвѣ поминанія и благословеніе.
units.english_cohort_translation: Note. It must be noted that at the end of Compline the troparia: “Have mercy on us, O Lord,” etc., and the litany: “Have mercy on us, O God,” and “Again we pray that this city may be preserved,” etc., in the Great Fast are taken neither at Small nor at Great Compline, except in Passion Week on Wednesday, Friday, and Saturday at Small Compline, as is our custom.

units.slavonic_incipit: δ) Чинъ Повечерія Великаго въ Пяткахъ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: чин повечерия великаго в пятках вел поста
units.slavonic_diplomatic: δ) Чинъ Повечерія Великаго въ Пяткахъ Вел. Поста.*) Повечеріе сіе есть безъ поклоновъ, ибо въ греческой Церкви поклоны въ Субботу не бываютъ. Оно сякъ отправляется: І. Часть. Начало обычайное съ Ѱалмами, съ „Съ нами Богъ“ и съ прочими моленіями даже до „Отче наш“-а. По семъ берется тропарь и то: въ Пятокъ І-ой седмицы тропарь св. мученика Ѳеодора; въ Пятки ІІ-ой, ІІІ-ой и IV-ой седмицы вел. Поста тропарь Мученикамъ и о Оусопшихъ; въ Пятокъ V-ой седмицы есть малое Повечеріе съ тропарями Акаѳиста и велик. Канона; въ Пятокъ VI-ой седмицы есть тропарь св. Лазаря. По данномъ тропарю слѣдуетъ Господи пом. 40. Слава и Нынѣ. Честнѣйшую, и Іерей возглашаетъ: „Молитвами св. Отецъ“ и пр. и молитвою: „Господи, Господи“ окончитъ І-ую часть. ІІ-ая часть отправляется обычайно даже до „Отче наш“-а. По семъ тропари: „Помилуй насъ Господи“ и пр. Далѣе Господи пом. 40. Слава и Нынѣ. Честнѣйшую. Іерей возглашаетъ: „Молитвами св. Отецъ нашихъ“ и пр. и молитвою: „Владыко Боже“ и пр. окончитъ ІІ-ую часть.
units.english_cohort_translation: (δ) Order of Great Compline on the Fridays of the Great Fast.[^111] This Compline is without prostrations, for in the Greek Church there are no prostrations on Saturday. It is celebrated thus: Part I. Ordinary beginning with the Psalms, with “God is with us,” and with the other petitions even unto “Our Father.” After this the troparion is taken, namely: on Friday of the 1st week, the troparion of the Holy Martyr Theodore; on Fridays of the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th weeks of the Great Fast, the troparion to the Martyrs and for the Departed; on Friday of the 5th week there is Small Compline with the troparia of the Akathist and of the Great Canon; on Friday of the 6th week there is the troparion of St. Lazarus. After the given troparion follows: “Lord, have mercy” (40 times), “Glory,” and “Now and,” “More honorable,” and the Priest proclaims: “Through the prayers of our holy Fathers,” etc., and with the prayer: “O Lord, Lord,” concludes the 1st part. Part II is celebrated in the ordinary manner even unto “Our Father.” After this the troparia: “Have mercy on us, O Lord,” etc. Then: “Lord, have mercy” (40 times), “Glory,” and “Now and,” “More honorable.” The Priest proclaims: “Through the prayers of our holy Fathers,” etc., and with the prayer: “O Master, God,” etc., concludes the 2nd part.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: ІІІ. часть начинается отъ „Прійдите покл. 3.“ По семъ Ѱалмъ 67. и 142-ый. „Слава въ вышнихъ“. Канонъ покойный настоящаго гласа, нѣкогда и два каноны. „Достойно“, но безъ поклоновъ. Трисвятое. Отче нашъ съ возгласомъ. „Господи силъ“**) не поемъ, но вмѣсто „Господи силъ“ берутся кондаки, и то: въ Пятокъ 1-ой седмицы кондакъ св. мученика Ѳеодора; въ Пятки 2-ой, 3-ой и 4-ой седмицы кондакъ о оусопшихъ: „Со святыми оупокой“; въ Пятокъ 5-ой седмицы и въ Середу 5-ой седмицы, понеже тогда малое Повечеріе есть, кондаки Субботы Акаѳиста и велик. Канона; въ Пятокъ 6-ой седмицы кондакъ св. Лазаря. По кондакѣ Господи пом. 40. „Иже на всякое время“. Честнѣйшую. „Именемъ Господнимъ благослови Отче“. И Іерей возглашаетъ: „Боже оущедри ны“ и пр., но поклоны не творитъ. По поклонахъ *) У Типиконѣ то читаемъ, что По Пяткахъ св. Четыредесятницы Повечеріе обычно поемъ малое. Великое чрезвычайно берется. Типикъ, стр. 216.
units.english_cohort_translation: Part III begins from “Come, let us worship” (thrice). After this the Psalms: 67 and the 142nd. “Glory to God in the highest.” The canon for the departed of the current tone, sometimes even two canons. “It is truly right,” but without prostrations. The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. “O Lord of hosts”[^112] we do not sing, but instead of “O Lord of hosts” the kontakia are taken, namely: on Friday of the 1st week, the kontakion of the Holy Martyr Theodore; on Fridays of the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th weeks, the kontakion for the departed: “With the Saints give rest”; on Friday of the 5th week and on Wednesday of the 5th week, since then there is Small Compline, the kontakia of the Saturday of the Akathist and of the Great Canon; on Friday of the 6th week, the kontakion of St. Lazarus. After the kontakion: “Lord, have mercy” (40 times), “Thou Who at all times,” “More honorable,” “In the name of the Lord bless, Father.” And the Priest proclaims: “God be merciful unto us,” etc., but makes no prostrations. After the prostrations there follow (the Trisagion, “Our Father,” “Lord, have mercy” [12 times] are omitted) the prayers: “O undefiled, unblemished,” and “And grant unto us,” “Our hope,” but without kneeling. (The prayer “O most merciful Master” is omitted.) The smallest dismissal, commemorations, and the blessing.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: манассия которою иерей читает пред царскими дверьми три
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Манассія, которою Іерей читаетъ предъ царскими дверьми. Три- святое. Отче нашъ съ возгласомъ. Кондакъ праздника. Господи пом. 40. Слава и Нынѣ. Честнѣйшую. Именемъ Господнимъ и пр.
units.english_cohort_translation: The Priest in phelonion and epitrachelion censes the holy sanctuary, opens the royal doors, censes the whole church, stands before the royal doors, and when the chanter says: “Command!” he begins: “O Lord, bless!” And he proclaims: “Glory to the holy...” — and thus follows: “Come, let us worship.” The Priest, having entered after this into the holy sanctuary, shuts the royal doors, and having divested of the phelonion, in the epitrachelion comes forth before the royal doors. The chanter meanwhile begins Part I of Great Compline, saying after “Come, let us worship” 3 psalms. The Priest goes into the holy sanctuary, and the chanter reads Psalms: 4, 6, 12 [Pss. 4, 6, 12]. “Glory,” and “Now and,” “Alleluia” (thrice), “Lord, have mercy” (thrice), “Glory,” and “Now and.” And immediately Psalms: 24, 30, and the 90th [Pss. 24, 30, 90]. “Glory,” and “Now and,” “Alleluia” (thrice), “Lord, have mercy” (thrice), “Glory,” and “Now and.” And immediately the Priest comes forth and sings once: “God is with us.” The choir repeats this 1st verse twice. After this the Priest, standing before the royal doors, reads the verses: “Unto the ends of the earth,” etc., and the choir after each verse sings: “God is with us,” etc. At the end the Priest again sings this first verse once, and the choir repeats it twice. After this canticle of the Prophet Isaiah there follows: “The day being past,” etc., “The bodiless nature,” “O Most Holy Virgin,” “I believe,” “O Most Holy Trinity,” each verse twice. After these: The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. The troparion of the feast (for instance, of the Nativity of Christ, the Theophany, or the Annunciation), and that once. “Lord, have mercy” (40 times), “Glory,” and “Now and,” “More honorable,” “In the name of the Lord,” etc. And the Priest proclaims: “Through the prayers of our holy Fathers,” etc., and with the prayer: “O Lord, Lord of hosts,” concludes Part I, having entered into the sanctuary. Part II begins from “Come, let us worship” (thrice), after which follow Psalms: 50 and the 101st [Pss. 50, 101]. The prayer of King Manasses, which the Priest reads before the royal doors. The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. The kontakion of the feast. “Lord, have mercy” (40 times), “Glory,” and “Now and,” “More honorable,” “In the name of the Lord,” etc., and the Priest proclaims: “O Lord Jesus Christ,” etc., and with the prayer: “O Master, God the Father,” etc., concludes Part II, having entered into the holy sanctuary. Part III begins from “Come, let us worship” (thrice). After this Psalms: 69 and the 142nd [Pss. 69, 142]. “Glory to God in the highest” is read. — Meanwhile the Priest vests in the phelonion, opens the royal doors, blesses the censer, and in the usual manner, as at the entrance, goes forth by the northern door, censes the entire church, and after the censing goes unto the table or *Tetrapod* in the midst of the church, where there are already prepared 5 loaves or prosphora, wheat, wine, and oil. The arrangement of the *Tetrapod* is thus: on the right side is placed the wine, on the left the oil, in the middle the wheat, and upon it 5 loaves (prosphora), and that four prosphora are placed cruciformly, and the fifth lies upon them touching all four. After this the choir after “Glory to God in the highest,” etc., sings the stichera at the Litiya (and that 5 with “Glory,” and “Now and”), and upon the conclusion of these the Priest chants the litany at the Litiya: “Save, O God, Thy people,” etc. After this, the stichera at the aposticha. Next: “Now Thou lettest depart.” The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. The troparion of the feast (thrice). (When the Priest sings the troparion, he at the same time also censes.) After the troparion the Priest proclaims: “Let us pray to the Lord,” and reads the prayer over the blessing of the loaves: “O Lord Jesus Christ,” etc., taking first the prosphora lying on top, and having then set it back in its place, with outstretched fingers he signs the entire oblation at the words: “Bless these loaves, the wheat, the wine, and the oil” with a single sign of the cross. After this prayer follows: “Blessed be the name of the Lord” (thrice), while the Priest censes the oblation, — and after this Psalm 33 [Ps. 33] is read up to “Shall not want any good thing.” The Priest goes unto the royal doors, and the chanter upon the conclusion of the psalm says: “Lord, have mercy” (thrice), “Glory,” and “Now and,” “In the name of the Lord bless, Father”; and the Priest standing before the royal doors, at the exclamation of the choir: “In the name of the Lord bless, Father,” begins Matins, saying: “Glory to the holy...” etc.[^113]

units.slavonic_incipit: Полунощница Субботная такъ отправляется, какъ и
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: лунощница субботная так отправляется как и повсед невная
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Полунощница Субботная такъ отправляется, какъ и Повсед- невная, лишь α) вмѣсто 17-ой кадизмы берется 9-ая кадизма, т. е. Ѱалмы: 64., 65., 66., 67., 68. и 69-ый. β) Вмѣсто тропа- рей: „Се женихъ“ и пр. читаются тропари въ честь пресв. Тройцы:
units.english_cohort_translation: The Saturday Midnight Office is celebrated in the same manner as the daily one, except that: (α) instead of the 17th Kathisma the 9th Kathisma is taken, that is to say, Psalms: 64, 65, 66, 67, 68, and the 69th [Pss. 64, 65, 66, 67, 68, 69]; (β) instead of the troparia: “Behold, the Bridegroom,” etc., there are read the troparia in honor of the Most Holy Trinity: “Uncreated nature”; finally (γ) instead of the prayer: “Those who hate,” etc., the prayer of St. Eustratius is taken: “Magnifying, I magnify Thee,” etc.

units.slavonic_incipit: Прійдите поклонимся 3. Подъ симъ Іерей
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: прийдите поклонимся 3 под сим иерей входит в
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Прійдите поклонимся 3. Подъ симъ Іерей входитъ въ св. олтарь, пѣвецъ же начинаетъ читати Ѱаломъ 50. По семъ (вмѣсто ка- дизмы) канонъ къ пресв. Тройцѣ, который находится въ Октоихѣ, при каждомъ гласѣ. По канонѣ же первѣе Тройчное Величаніе, со- стоящее изъ больше тропарей („Достойно есть богоподобнѣ“, „Господоначалную Херувимовъ“, „Отцу безначальну и Богу“, „Во- споимъ вси“, „Лучезарнымъ“, „Егоже трепещутъ“, „Достойно есть благоговѣйно“, „Прійми слезы“, Слава: „Отче Вседержителю“, а на конецъ И нынѣ: „Изъ мертвыхъ“). По семъ поется Величаніе
units.english_cohort_translation: If it be celebrated in church, then: The Priest, having put on the epitrachelion, makes before the royal doors the usual beginning: “Blessed is our God,” etc. The choir: “Amen,” and immediately: “O Heavenly King,” The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. “Lord, have mercy” (12 times), “Come, let us worship” (thrice). During this the Priest enters into the holy sanctuary, and the chanter begins to read Psalm 50 [Ps. 50]. After this (instead of the kathisma), the canon to the Most Holy Trinity, which is found in the Octoechos under each tone. After the canon, first the Triadicon Megalynarion, consisting of several troparia (“It is truly meet to praise Thee, Who art God,” “The Chief of the Cherubim,” “Unto the unoriginate Father and God,” “Let us all sing,” “With radiant,” “Before Whom tremble,” “It is truly meet reverently,” “Receive tears,” “Glory,” “O Father Almighty,” and at the end “Now and,” “From the dead”). After this is sung the Megalynarion of the Theotokos: “It is truly right,” and thus: The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation and (among us) the Troparia:[^115] “Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us,” and the litany: “Have mercy on us, O God,” etc., with the exclamation: “Hear us, O God.” After the litany the smallest dismissal, and that the resurrectional one (“Christ, our true God, Who rose from the dead,” etc.). Commemorations. (The commemoration for the departed is omitted.) The prayer: “Remit, forgive,” etc., and the prayer to the Most Holy Trinity: “All-powerful and life-creating,” and thus the blessing.

units.slavonic_incipit: Если же Полунощница Недѣльная чтется на
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: если же полунощница недельная чтется на едине тогда
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Если же Полунощница Недѣльная чтется на единѣ, тогда чтется канонъ общій Тройченъ, списанъ въ Молитвословѣ, а на концѣ по тропаряхъ „Помилуй насъ Господи“ не глаголется ек- тенія: „Помилуй насъ Боже“ и пр., но вмѣсто нея Господи пом.
units.english_cohort_translation: If, however, the Sunday Midnight Office is read in private, then there is read the general Triadicon canon, recorded in the *Molitvoslov*, and at the end after the troparia “Have mercy on us, O Lord” the litany: “Have mercy on us, O God,” etc., is not said, but instead of it: “Lord, have mercy” (40 times), “Glory,” and “Now and,” “Lord, have mercy” (thrice), “Lord, bless,” and the Dismissal. And thus the prayer: “All-powerful and life-creating,” etc.

units.slavonic_incipit: Полунощница, лишь то потребно замѣтити, что
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: лунощница лиш то потребно заметити что на конце
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Полунощница, лишь то потребно замѣтити, что на концѣ І-ой части, по „Боже оущедри ны“ и проч. и междъ молитвою: „Вла- дыко Боже Отче“ суть поклоны съ молитвою св. Ефрема: „Го- споди и Владыко“ и пр. И то есть: α) великіи три съ молитвою св. Ефрема. (Великій поклонъ есть, когда человѣкъ падаетъ колѣ- нами и главу приклоняетъ до земли на сколько можетъ.) β) 12 меньшихъ поклоновъ (съ стихами: „Боже милостивъ буди мнѣ грѣшному“. „Боже очисти грѣхи мои и помилуй мя“. И „Безъ числа согрѣшихъ Господи, прости мя“.) По молитвѣ: „Владыко
units.english_cohort_translation: It is celebrated in the same manner as the daily Midnight Office at other times, except that it is necessary to note that at the end of Part I, after “God be merciful unto us,” etc., and before the prayer: “O Master, God the Father,” there are prostrations with the prayer of St. Ephrem: “O Lord and Master,” etc. And that is: (α) three great prostrations with the prayer of St. Ephrem. (A great prostration is when a man falls upon his knees and bows his head unto the earth as far as he can.) (β) 12 lesser prostrations (with the verses: “O God, be merciful unto me a sinner”; “O God, cleanse my sins and have mercy on me”; and “Without number have I sinned, O Lord, forgive me”). After the prayer: “O Master, God the Father,” again one great prostration. The rest in the usual manner.

units.english_cohort_translation: If a certain feast of the Lord, or a feast of the Mother of God, or a feast of a great Saint, or the Afterfeast of the Nativity of Christ and the Theophany fall upon weekdays whereon Litiya is not celebrated: then the Midnight Office is celebrated in the same manner as the daily Midnight Office, except that: (α) the troparion: “Behold, the Bridegroom,” etc., is omitted, and instead of these the troparion of the feast is sung; (β) the troparion and prayer for the departed are omitted, and instead of them the kontakion of the feast is sung. Upon the conclusion of the kontakion there are sung among us the Troparia: “Have mercy on us, O Lord,” etc., and the litany: “Have mercy on us, O God,” etc., with the exclamation: “Hear us, O God.”[^116] Dismissal. Commemorations. (The commemoration for the departed is omitted.) Blessing. (The last two prayers are omitted.)

units.slavonic_incipit: Отче нашъ. Прійдите покл. 3. Ѱаломъ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: отче наш прийдите покл 3 псалом 50 и
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Отче нашъ. Прійдите покл. 3. Ѱаломъ 50. И слѣдуетъ канонъ оутренный Великой Субботы: „Волною морскою“. По канонѣ вмѣсто „Достойно есть“ Ірмосъ: „Не рыдай мене Мати“. И абіе: Три- святое. Отче нашъ съ возгласомъ. Тропари „Егда снизшелъ еси“.
units.english_cohort_translation: Before the Resurrection of Christ, likewise before midnight, there is to be celebrated the Midnight Office, or the so-called “Burial Service” (*Nadhrobne*). And that in the following order: The Priest, vested in a black epitrachelion, before the royal doors begins the Midnight Office with: “Blessed is our God.” After this the choir: “Amen,” “O Heavenly King,” “Our Father,” “Come, let us worship” (thrice). Psalm 50 [Ps. 50]. And there follows the Matins canon of Great Saturday: “By a wave of the sea.” After the canon, instead of “It is truly right,” the Heirmos: “Weep not for Me, O Mother.” And immediately: The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. Troparia: “When Thou didst descend,” “The noble Joseph,” and “Unto the Myrrhbearers.” After these the Priest goes from the royal doors unto the Tomb, and having bowed, censes the Shroud (*Plashchanytsia*), and after this transfers It unto the holy table, where he spreads It out and again censes It. After this he says the litany: “Have mercy on us, O God,” etc., as at the Sunday Midnight Office. Dismissal.

units.english_cohort_translation: Great Matins, however, is celebrated on feasts and on Sundays. And in accordance with this it is: Festal and Sunday. But since feasts are of two kinds: those with the Doxology and those with the Polyeleos, so also festal Matins services are of two kinds, that is to say: (α) with the Doxology, but without the Polyeleos; (β) with both the Doxology and the Polyeleos.

units.slavonic_incipit: По изреченіи трехъ Ѱалмовъ: Слава и
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: изречении трех псалмов слава и ныне аллилуя
units.slavonic_diplomatic: По изреченіи трехъ Ѱалмовъ: Слава и Нынѣ. Аллилуя 3. Господи *) Если же была въ церкви Полунощница, то по „Благословенъ Богъ нашъ“ абіе слѣдуетъ „Прійдите покл. 3.“ пом. 3. Слава и Нынѣ. По совершенію же шестопсалмія: Слава и Нынѣ. Аллилуя 3. Слава Тебѣ Боже, (третіе съ пѣніемъ.) По семъ
units.english_cohort_translation: If there be no Midnight Office in church,[^117] then the Priest, having entered into the church, makes three bows before the royal doors, and having kissed and put on the epitrachelion, begins in the usual manner: “Blessed is our God.” The choir: “Amen,” and immediately: “O Heavenly King,” The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. “Lord, have mercy” (12 times), “Come, let us worship” (thrice). Psalms: 19 and the 20th [Pss. 19, 20], after which: “Glory,” and “Now and.” The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. And after this the reader says the troparion: “Save, O Lord, Thy people,” etc., “Glory,” “Thou Who wast voluntarily lifted up upon the Cross,” etc., “Now and,” Theotokion: “O fearsome defense,” etc. Upon the conclusion of these troparia the Priest proclaims the litany: “Have mercy on us, O God,” etc., “Furthermore let us pray for our most devout Emperor,” etc., unto which petitions the choir answers: “Lord, have mercy” (6 times). Then the exclamation: “For a merciful and man-befriending God art Thou,” etc. Whereunto the choir answers: “Amen,” and immediately proclaims aloud: “In the name of the Lord bless, Father.” And the Priest proclaims: “Glory to the holy, consubstantial, and life-creating...” etc. The choir: “Amen,” and begins first: “Glory to God in the highest” (thrice), after this: “O Lord, open Thou my lips,” etc. (twice). And in order it says the Six Psalms (that is to say, Psalms: 3, 37, 62, 87, 102, and the 142nd [Pss. 3, 37, 62, 87, 102, 142]) in a quiet voice. After the recitation of three Psalms: “Glory,” and “Now and,” “Alleluia” (thrice), “Lord, have mercy” (thrice), “Glory,” and “Now and.” Upon the completion of the Six Psalms: “Glory,” and “Now and,” “Alleluia” (thrice), “Glory to Thee, O God” (the third time with chanting). After this the Priest, standing before the royal doors, says the litany of peace: “In peace let us pray to the Lord.” After its exclamation the Priest sings: “God is the Lord, and hath appeared unto us,” etc., and the chanter repeats it 4 times (according to the verses). The Priest, having bowed, withdraws unto his place, and there secretly recites the morning prayers; and the chanter begins to sing the troparia, and that: the troparion of the Saint (twice); “Glory,” and “Now and,” the dismissal Theotokion according to the tone of the Saint (or as the typikon prescribes). After the troparia follows: Kathisma 1. The 1st Sessional Hymn with the Theotokion. Kathisma 2. The 2nd Sessional Hymn. (Before the kathisma, both the 1st and the 2nd, the choir says: “Lord, have mercy” [thrice] and “Glory,” and the reader continues from “Now and.” After the kathisma: “Lord, have mercy” [twice], “To Thee, O Lord,” “Amen.”) After the 2nd Sessional Hymn and after “Lord, have mercy” (thrice), “Glory,” and “Now and,” the chanter reads Psalm 50 [Ps. 50]. After this the canons, usually 3 (two from the Octoechos, and one of the Saint). The troparia in the canons are read with the appropriate refrains, and that: let there be 14 troparia in all with “Glory,” and with “Now and.” The heirmoi are taken from the first canon. The heirmoi from the canon of the Saint are taken as the Katavasia, but only after the 3rd, 6th, 8th, and 9th odes. After the 3rd ode there is the small litany and the Sessional Hymn from the Common Menaion, that is to say, of the Saint. — After the 6th ode, the small litany, the kontakion and ikos of the Saint. Towards the end of the 8th ode instead of “Glory” we say: “We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord”; before the Katavasia the choir says in the tone of the canon of the Saint: “We praise, we bless, we worship,” etc., and they sing the Heirmos of the 8th ode of the canon of the Saint as Katavasia. After the 8th ode the Priest in the sanctuary proclaims: “The Theotokos and Mother of Light in hymns let us magnify,” whereunto the choir loudly sings: “My soul doth magnify the Lord,” etc., chanting unto the verses: “More honorable than the Cherubim,” etc. After the Katavasia of the 9th ode: “It is truly right.” The small litany and the Exaposteilarion, and that of the day; “Glory,” of the Saint; “Now and,” Theotokion, or if it be Wednesday or Friday: Stavrotheotokion. And immediately Psalms: 148, 149, and the 150th [Pss. 148, 149, 150] are read (“Praise the Lord from the heavens,” “Sing unto the Lord a new song,” and “Praise God in His Saints”). Upon the conclusion of Psalm 150, the Priest proclaims from the sanctuary: “Glory to God Who hath shown us the light,” and the choir reads the Doxology in order: “Glory to God in the highest.”[^118]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Богородиченъ отпустительный по гласу Святаго. Іерей по семъ выходитъ изъ олтаря и передъ царскими дверми поетъ ектенію:
units.english_cohort_translation: After this the Priest comes forth from the sanctuary and before the royal doors says the litany: “Let us complete our morning prayer.” After the 2nd exclamation of this litany the Priest enters into the sanctuary, and the choir begins to sing the stichera at the aposticha (from the Octoechos) with the usual refrains. (Before the 1st there is no verse; before the 2nd and 3rd: “We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy,” and “Let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us” [Ps. 89:14, 17]). At the end: “Glory,” and “Now and,” Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion.[^119] After this the choir reads: “It is good to give praise,” The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. After this the troparion of the Saint. “Glory,” and “Now and,” the dismissal Theotokion according to the tone of the Saint. The Priest after this comes forth from the sanctuary and before the royal doors chants the litany: “Have mercy on us, O God.” The daily dismissal, and that the small one, and the blessing.

units.slavonic_incipit: *) Въ Субботу предваряютъ канонъ Святаго
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: в субботу предваряют канон святаго и по
units.slavonic_diplomatic: *) Въ Субботу предваряютъ канонъ Святаго и по немъ храма Святаго, таже въ Октоиху мучениченъ. (Покоинъ же канонъ поется въ Пятокъ на Повечеріи.) На Хвалитехъ въ Субботу стихиры не поемъ въ Октоиху, но поемъ ихъ на Стиховнѣхъ мученичны 3 съ припѣвами обычными. Субботніи же стиховны оставляются и они лишь въ задушныя Субботы поются съ упокойными ихъ припивами. (Сія перемѣна съ стихирами на Стиховнѣхъ бываетъ и въ Пятокъ вечеръ на Вечерни.) Типикъ, стр. 53.
units.english_cohort_translation: (α) Matins with the Great Doxology. This Matins is celebrated on minor feasts, that is to say, when the feast or the Saint hath stichera on 6 and the Great Doxology. Beginning from the start, up unto the Doxology, it is small,[^120] and only here towards the end of the Praises (*Ainoi*) the Priest vests in the epitrachelion and phelonion, and stands before the Holy Table, awaiting the end of the stichera at the Praises. — When the chanter hath concluded these, then he opens the royal doors and proclaims: “Glory to God, Who hath shown us the light,” and goes forth onto the ambo and there with the chanter sings the Doxology.[^121] After this The Trisagion (thrice). And immediately the troparion of the feast with the Theotokion, after which the Priest enters unto the Holy Table and there chants the litanies: “Have mercy on us, O God,” and “Let us complete.”

units.slavonic_incipit: **) Передъ каѳизмою и по каѳизмѣ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: перед кафизмою и по кафизме все так
units.slavonic_diplomatic: **) Передъ каѳизмою и по каѳизмѣ все такъ глаголется якъ сказанно было выше.
units.english_cohort_translation: (β) Matins with the Polyeleos, with the Gospel, and with the Great Doxology. It is celebrated on weekdays if there occur a Saint having a polyeleos, or a feast of the Lord, or a feast of the Mother of God. The order of this Matins is as follows: The Priest, having put on the epitrachelion, comes before the royal doors, and having made a bow there, says: “Blessed is our God.” The choir: “Amen.” Then (if there was no Midnight Office): “O Heavenly King.” After this also the rest of the usual beginning. After “Come, let us worship” (thrice), Psalms: 19 and the 20th [Pss. 19, 20]. And immediately The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. After this the troparia are read: “Save, O God, Thy people,” etc., after which the litany for the Emperor with the exclamation. Unto the exclamation the choir answers: “Amen,” and immediately proclaims: “In the name of the Lord bless, Father.” Unto this the Priest: “Glory to the holy...” etc. The choir: “Amen,” and immediately: “Glory to God in the highest,” etc. (thrice), “O Lord, open Thou my lips,” etc. (twice). And there follows the Six Psalms. (The Priest enters into the holy sanctuary and recites the priestly morning prayers.) After the Six Psalms the Priest comes forth and the litany of peace is chanted. “God is the Lord, and hath appeared unto us,” etc. (4 times). Festal troparia. Kathisma 1. The 1st Sessional Hymn of the Saint. Kathisma 2. The 2nd Sessional Hymn of the Saint.[^123] After this: “Glory,” and “Now and,” Theotokion, and instead of the 3rd kathisma the choir sings the Polyeleos (that is to say, verses from the 19th Kathisma: “Praise the name of the Lord,” etc.). After this: The Megalynarion with the verses. After this the small litany is said and the choir sings the 3rd Sessional Hymn (the polyeleos one), “Glory,” and “Now and,” Theotokion. Then the Gradual Hymns of the 4th Tone, the 1st Antiphon: “From my youth,” which are sung to 4 verses, chanting unto the 3rd verse “Glory,” and unto the 4th “Now and.” During the singing of the 3rd and 4th verses, that is to say, at “Glory,” and “Now and,” the Priest vests in the phelonion, ascends unto the Holy Table, and proclaims: “Let us attend! Peace be to all! Wisdom, let us attend!” Then the choir sings the daily Prokimenon. After the Prokimenon the Priest opens the royal doors, saying: “Let us pray to the Lord.” Unto this the choir: “Lord, have mercy,” and immediately the Priest says the exclamation: “For holy art Thou,” etc. The choir: “Amen.” And again the Priest: “Let every breath praise the Lord,” and censes the Holy Table and from the royal doors the people. After the choir sings: “Let every breath praise the Lord” twice, the Priest [says]: “That we may be accounted worthy to hear the holy Gospel,” etc. Then upon the choir’s response the Priest [says]: “Peace be to all!” The choir: (“And to thy spirit”). And thereafter: “Wisdom, let us attend, let us hear the holy Gospel,” etc., and he reads the holy Gospel, and that standing before the Holy Table. After the Gospel hath been read, immediately Psalm 50 [Ps. 50]. (The Priest, after reading the holy Gospel, goes forth and gives the holy Gospel to be kissed upon the ambo.) — After Psalm 50: “Glory”: “Through the prayers of the holy Archangel [or: holy Apostle, or: Prophet],” etc. ([Name]), in whose honor the service is celebrated. At “Now and”: “Through the prayers of the Most Holy Theotokos,” etc., is sung. At the end the refrain: “Have mercy on me, O God,” etc., and the sticheron of the Saint.[^124] After this the Priest, having returned unto the Holy Table, chants the litany: “Save, O God, Thy people,” etc., whereunto the choir [responds]: “Lord, have mercy” (thrice). And immediately the Priest: “Lord, have mercy” (thrice), whereunto the choir again: “Lord, have mercy” (thrice). And immediately the Priest [says] the exclamation: “Through the mercy and compassions...”[^125] etc. After this exclamation the Priest shuts the royal doors, divests of the phelonion, and the chanter begins to sing the canon on 14. In the canon all things are taken in order. Before the Katavasia of the 8th ode the choir proclaims the refrain: “We praise, we bless, we worship,” etc., and sings the Katavasia. After the Katavasia the Priest proclaims: “The Theotokos and Mother of Light,” etc., and the magnification of the feast is sung (that is, the Heirmos of the 9th ode with the refrain) or “More honorable than the Cherubim.”[^126] After the 9th ode: the small litany and the Exaposteilarion. Stichera at the Praises (*Ainoi*): and that we set 4; “Glory,” of the Saint; “Now and,” Theotokion. At this the Priest vests in the phelonion, opens the royal doors, and goes forth onto the ambo, and proclaims: “Glory to God, Who hath shown us the light”; they sing the Great Doxology. The Trisagion. The troparion of the Saint and Theotokion. The Priest, having entered into the sanctuary, says before the Holy Table the litanies: “Have mercy on us, O God,” and “Let us complete.” The great dismissal, the blessing, and he shuts the royal doors.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: По семъ: „Господи пом. 2. Тебѣ Господи. Аминь“, и абіе Сѣда- ленъ 2-ый съ „Слава и Нынѣ“ на что спѣвается Богородиченъ его. По Сѣдалномъ 2-ымъ, какъ первѣе читаетъ чтецъ кадизму 3-ю, (сія есть 17-а: „Блаженни непорочніи“), или поетъ полуелей.*)
units.english_cohort_translation: It is celebrated thus: The beginning is the usual one, as at daily Matins without any exception. After the Six Psalms, when the choir sings: “Alleluia” (thrice), “Glory to Thee, O God,” the Priest, standing before the royal doors, says the litany of peace. After this: “God is the Lord, and hath appeared unto us,” etc., which chant is sung in the current tone. The resurrectional (Sunday) troparion (twice); “Glory,” of the Saint; “Now and,” Theotokion from the Octoechos according to the tone of the Saint. After the troparia the choir immediately says: “Lord, have mercy” (thrice), and “Glory”; the reader continues: “Now and,” and reads Kathisma 1. After the kathisma: “Lord, have mercy” (twice), “To Thee, O Lord,” “Amen”; and immediately the 1st Sessional Hymn from the Octoechos is sung, first plain, and thereafter unto the refrain: “Arise, O Lord my God,” etc., and at the end with “Glory,” and “Now and.” After the 1st Sessional Hymn the choir: “Lord, have mercy” (thrice), “Glory”; the reader: “Now and,” and reads the 2nd Kathisma. After this: “Lord, have mercy” (twice), “To Thee, O Lord,” “Amen”; and immediately the 2nd Sessional Hymn with “Glory,” and “Now and,” whereunto its Theotokion is sung. After the 2nd Sessional Hymn, as before, the reader reads the 3rd Kathisma (this is the 17th: “Blessed are the undefiled”), or [the choir] sings the Polyeleos.[^127] But instead of the 3rd Sessional Hymn the troparia after the Evlogitaria (*Neporochny*) are sung: “The angelic host,” with the refrain: “Blessed art Thou, O Lord: teach me Thy statutes.” After this: the small litany. The Hypakoe of the tone. The Gradual Hymns (*Stepenny*). After the Gradual Hymns the Priest, vested in the phelonion, proclaims from the Holy Table: “Let us attend! Peace be to all! Wisdom, let us attend!” and the choir sings the Prokimenon. After the Prokimenon the Priest opens the royal doors, saying: “Let us pray to the Lord.” Whereunto the choir answers: “Lord, have mercy,” and immediately he proclaims: “For holy art Thou, O our God,” etc. Again after this exclamation the Priest says once: “Let every breath praise the Lord,” and the chanter [says it] twice. After this the Priest begins to cense the Holy Table and the people from the royal doors, and proclaims: “That we may be accounted worthy,” etc.; further: “Peace be to all!” The choir: “And to thy spirit.” Then the Priest: “Wisdom, let us attend, let us hear the holy Gospel,” the reading from the holy Gospel according to Mark (or Matthew, or Luke, or John), and he reads the holy Gospel before the Holy Table. Upon the conclusion of the Gospel the Priest reads before the Holy Table: “Having seen the Resurrection of Christ.” The chanter after this reads Psalm 50 [Ps. 50], during which the Priest comes forth from the sanctuary onto the ambo and gives the holy Gospel to be kissed. After Psalm 50 the chanter sings: “Glory”: “Through the prayers of the holy Apostles,” etc.; “Now and”: “Through the prayers of the Most Holy Theotokos,” etc. Then unto “Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great [mercy],” etc., the resurrectional sticheron[^128] is sung in the 6th Tone (“Jesus, having risen from the tomb”). And immediately the Priest says the litany: “Save, O God, Thy people,” etc. After this: “Lord, have mercy” (thrice). Exclamation: “Through the mercy and compassions,” etc. After this the Priest shuts the royal doors, and the choir sings the canons; and that: the Resurrectional, Cross-Resurrectional, and Theotokion from the Octoechos.[^129] Only the heirmoi and katavasiai are sung, while the other troparia are read. The troparia of the canons are read on 14 with the proper refrains in order, as was stated. — Before the Katavasia of the 8th ode the chanter proclaims aloud: “We praise, we bless, we worship the Lord, singing and exalting Him unto all ages.” After the 8th ode the Priest proclaims: “The Theotokos and Mother of Light,” etc.,[^130] and the choir sings: “My soul doth magnify [the Lord],” refraining: “More honorable than the Cherubim,” etc., with the verses. After the 9th ode the small litany, and immediately the Priest, having come forth before the royal doors, proclaims: “Holy is the Lord our God” (thrice). The choir likewise answers thrice. After this the Exaposteilarion. At the Praises (*Ainoi*) the choir sings: “Let every breath praise the Lord; praise Him in the highest; to Thee song is due, O God”; and the second verse of Psalm 148 [Ps. 148] with this ending according to the current tone. The other verses of the psalm are read from the 148th and the 149th [Pss. 148, 149]. We set 8 verses from the last verse of Psalm 149 [Ps. 149]: “This glory shall be to all His saints.” And we sing the resurrectional and Anatolian (*vostochny*) stichera with the refrains taken from Psalm 150 [Ps. 150], and with the two resurrectional ones: “Arise, O Lord my God,” etc., and “I will give thanks unto Thee, O Lord,” etc. After this: “Glory,” the Gospel sticheron; “Now and,” “Most blessed art thou.” The Priest vests in the phelonion, goes forth before the Holy Table, and makes a bow before the Holy Table. Upon the conclusion of the singing he opens the royal doors, goes forth onto the ambo, makes a bow, and proclaims aloud: “Glory to God, Who hath shown us the light.” The chanter goes unto the midst of the church, and together with the congregation the Great Doxology is sung. After the Doxology the Priest sings the Trisagion once, and the chanter twice. Then the resurrectional troparion by both, and that: if it be the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Евангелій воскресныхъ, 11 стихиръ евангелскихъ, и 11 Свѣтил- ныхъ воскресныхъ, которіи въ смыслѣ сходны суть. Кромѣ сего тѣ суть свойства сей оутрени недѣльной, что она по большой части не имѣетъ полуелея, но имѣетъ тропари воскресніи по не- порочныхъ, на ней „Воскресеніе Христово“ по Евангеліи читается, и на конецъ имѣетъ „Святъ Господь Богъ нашъ“.
units.english_cohort_translation: tone: “Today salvation is come unto the world”; but if it be the 2nd, 4th, 6th, and 8th Tone, then: “Having risen from the tomb” (*Molitvoslov*, p. 424). After this the Priest, having bowed, enters into the holy sanctuary, and takes the Gospel from the *Tetrapod*, if it was there. After this the Priest, standing before the Holy Table, says the litanies: “Have mercy on us, O God,” and “Let us complete our morning [prayer],” etc. At the end he makes the great dismissal, commemorating also the Saint in whose honor the service is sung, and gives the blessing. After the dismissal he shuts the royal doors.

units.english_cohort_translation: Note: At Sunday Matins there are taken in order 11 resurrectional Gospels, 11 Gospel stichera, and 11 resurrectional Exaposteilaria, which agree in meaning.
