units.slavonic_incipit: По семъ ектенія малая о оусопшихъ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: сем ектения малая о оусопших паки паки
units.slavonic_diplomatic: По семъ ектенія малая о оусопшихъ („Паки, паки миромъ Господу помолимся“. „Еще молимся о оставленіи согрѣшеній въ блажен- нѣй памяти преставшимся рабомъ Божіимъ“ и пр. И возгласъ:
units.english_cohort_translation: This Matins is small, without the Gospel and without the Great Doxology. It is celebrated thus: The beginning is the usual one, only that after the Six Psalms, instead of the litany of peace, the litany for the departed is taken (*Molitvoslov*, p. 328). Instead of: “God is the Lord,” etc., “Alleluia” (4 times), and immediately there are sung in the 8th Tone the troparia: “With profound wisdom,” “Glory,” and “Now and”: “Thee, the rampart.” After the troparia, the usual 1st Kathisma, and the 1st Sessional Hymn from the Octoechos. Immediately after the 1st Sessional Hymn: “Blessed are the undefiled” is sung in two stases; and that the first stasis with the refrain: “Blessed art Thou,” etc., and at the end of this stasis the verse: “Unless Thy law had been,” etc. (thrice). After this the small litany for the departed (“Again and again in peace let us pray to the Lord”; “Furthermore let us pray for the remission of sins of the servants of God departed in blessed memory,” etc. And the exclamation: “For Thou art the resurrection,” etc. [See *Molitvoslov*, p. 355]), and immediately the second stasis begins to be sung: “I am Thine.” After these two stases follow the troparia: “The choir of the Saints,” with the refrain: “Blessed art Thou, O Lord.” After the troparia, the litany for the departed,[^131] and thus only the 2nd Sessional Hymn (“Give rest, O our Savior”). After the 2nd Sessional Hymn, Psalm 50 [Ps. 50]. After this the canon of the temple with the Heirmos on 6, and the canon from the Triodion on 8. After the 3rd ode of the canon the usual litany, and not for the departed. After the 6th ode the litany for the departed, and the kontakion: “With the Saints.” After the 9th the usual litany, and not for the departed, and the Exaposteilarion: “Ruling over the living and the dead,” etc. All the rest in order. At the Praises (*Ainoi*) 4 stichera from the Triodion; “Glory,” and “Now and,” likewise from the Triodion. The Small Doxology. After this the litany: “Let us complete our morning [prayer],” etc. Stichera at the aposticha for the departed with verses for the departed, and with “Glory,” and “Now and.” Psalm: “It is good to give praise.” The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. The troparion for the departed: “With profound wisdom”; “Glory,” and “Now and”: “Thee, the rampart.” The litany for the departed (*Molitvoslov*, p. 355). The Dismissal.[^132] The blessing, and thus the Priest proclaims: “In blessed falling asleep, eternal rest...” etc. The choir: “Memory eternal.” — This Matins is celebrated on All Souls Saturdays.

units.slavonic_incipit: ***) Суть же α) въ Понедѣлокъ:
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: сут же в понеделок заступлением безплотных
units.slavonic_diplomatic: ***) Суть же α) въ Понедѣлокъ: „Заступленіемъ Безплотныхъ твоихъ помилуй насъ“: β) Въ Вторникъ: „Молитвами Предтечи помилуй насъ“. γ) Въ Середу и Пятокъ: „Силою Креста Твоего сохрани насъ“. δ) Въ Четверь: „Молитвами св. Апостолъ и Святителя Николая помилуй насъ“. — (2-ый и 3-ый Тройченъ однако окончиваются.)
units.english_cohort_translation: (α) Order of Daily Matins in the Holy Great Fast with the First Hour (excepting Saturdays and Sundays). It begins: “Blessed is our God”; but if there was no Midnight Office in church, then: “Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.” “O Heavenly King.” The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. “Lord, have mercy” (12 times). “Come, let us worship” (thrice).[^133] Psalms: 19 and the 20th [Pss. 19, 20], and all the rest in order. “God is the Lord” is not sung, but instead of that “Alleluia” (thrice) with 4 verses. (On Saturday, Sunday, and on feasts “God is the Lord” is sung.) Instead of the troparia, the 3 Triadica are sung slowly, and that in such a manner that at the 2nd verse “Glory” is taken, and at the 3rd “Now and.” — Let it be noted that at the end of the 1st Triadicon of all the 8 tones the endings of the day are said.[^134] (These endings are given in the *Horologion*, and in the *Molitvoslov*, p. 107.) After the Triadica, Kathisma 1. The 1st Sessional Hymn. After this: Kathisma 2. The 2nd Sessional Hymn. (These ses- sional hymns are the penitential ones of the Octoechos which are found at the end of the Menaion, and the martyr hymn (*Martyrikon*) with the refrain: “Wondrous is God in His Saints.” Besides this, let us also note that in the Great Fast neither after the 1st nor after the 2nd Kathisma is the small litany said, but the choir says: “Alleluia” (thrice), “Lord, have mercy” (thrice), “Glory,” and “Now and.”) After the 2nd Sessional Hymn the chanter says: “Lord, have mercy” (thrice), “Glory,” and “Now and,” and thus reads Psalm 50 [Ps. 50], and immediately the Priest comes forth before the royal doors and says the litany: “Save, O God, Thy people,” etc., with the exclamation: “Through the mercy and compassions.” After this litany follows the canon combined with the Biblical Odes (*Canticles of Moses*).[^135] In the Great Fast on weekdays there are 2 canons: of the Octoechos for the day with the Heirmos on 8, and of the Menaion for the Saint on 6. In whichever odes the Triodion (*Triodion-canon / Trepesnets*) occurs, we omit the canon of the Octoechos with the Heirmos, and sing the canon of the Saint with the Heirmos on 6, and the Triodion on 8. At the end the Katavasia is sung, and that the Heirmos of the Triodion canon.[^136] The Katavasia on weekdays throughout the entire Forty Days is sung thus: On Monday after the 1st, 3rd, 6th, 8th, and 9th ode. — On Tuesday after the 2nd, 3rd, 6th, 8th, and 9th ode. — On Wednesday after the 3rd, 6th, 8th, and 9th ode. — On Thursday after the 4th, 6th, 8th, and 9th ode. — On Friday after the 3rd, 5th, 6th, 8th, and 9th ode. — On Saturday after the 3rd, 6th, 7th, 8th, and 9th ode. After the 3rd ode, the Sessional Hymn of the Saint; “Glory,” and “Now and,” Theotokion. After the 6th, the kontakion and ikos of the Saint. (If, however, the Saint hath no kontakion in the Menaion, then here the martyr sessional hymn printed at the end of the Lenten Triodion is said.) After the 8th ode, at the exclamation of the Priest: “The Theotokos and Mother of Light,” etc., “My soul doth magnify [the Lord]” and “More honorable than the Cherubim.” After the 9th ode: “It is truly right” is sung with one bow. The small litany. The Lenten Exaposteilaria according to the 8 tones with the proper endings (*Molitvoslov*, pp. 137 and 106).

units.slavonic_incipit: Господи пом. 40. Господи благослови, подъ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: господи пом 40 господи благослови под которым иерей
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Господи пом. 40. Господи благослови, подъ которымъ Іерей вы- ходитъ передъ царскія двери и возглашаетъ: „Сый благословенъ и препрославленъ Христосъ Богъ нашъ“ и глаголетъ молитву: „Не- бесный Царю“. По семъ Господи пом. 3. Слава и Нынѣ. „Честнѣй- шую“ и „Именемъ Господнимъ благослови Отче“, и Іерей возгла- шаетъ: „Молитвами св. Отецъ нашихъ“ и пр. и чинитъ поклоны 3 съ молитвою св. Єфрема. — И абіе начинается часъ I-ый отъ „Прійдите поклонимся“, о немже слово будетъ позднѣе.
units.english_cohort_translation: The Praises (*Ainoi*) are read.[^137] After this the Priest says the exclamation: “To Thee glory is due,” etc., and immediately: “Glory to Thee Who hast shown us the light.” At this “Glory to God in the highest,” etc., is read. After this the Priest before the royal doors proclaims the litany: “Let us complete.” Stichera at the aposticha from the Triodion with the usual refrains, and the martyr hymn (*Martyrikon*); “Glory,” and “Now and,” Theotokion.[^138] After this: “It is good to give praise” (twice), etc. The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. The troparion: “Standing in the temple of Thy glory,” is read. After this (instead of the litany: “Have mercy on us, O God,” etc.): “Lord, have mercy” (40 times), “Lord, bless,” during which the Priest comes forth before the royal doors and proclaims: “Blessed and glorified is Christ our God,” and says the prayer: “O Heavenly King.” After this: “Lord, have mercy” (thrice), “Glory,” and “Now and,” “More honorable,” and “In the name of the Lord bless, Father”; and the Priest proclaims: “Through the prayers of our holy Fathers,” etc., and makes 3 prostrations with the prayer of St. Ephrem. — And immediately the First Hour begins from “Come, let us worship,” whereof mention will be made later.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: воскресение христово оставляется псалом 50 с стихирами праздника
units.slavonic_diplomatic: („Воскресеніе Христово“ оставляется. Ѱаломъ 50.) съ стихирами праздника. Послѣ которыхъ Іерей возглашаетъ ектенію: „Спаси Боже люди твоя“ и пр. съ возгласомъ „Милостію и щедротами“. По екте- ніи канонъ праздника совокупляется съ Трипѣснецемъ. Ірмосъ праз- дника, а катавасія рядовая. На „Богородицу и Матерь Свѣта“ величаніе праздника. По окончаніи канона свѣтиленъ праздникъ и сей- часъ стихиры на „Хвалите“-хъ праздникъ. Предъ Славословіемъ Іерей возглашаетъ: „Тебѣ слава подобаетъ“ и пр., по семъ глаголетъ:
units.english_cohort_translation: (β) Order of Festal Matins in the Great Fast, if a feast fall upon weekdays (excepting Saturdays and Sundays). — This Matins is great up unto the Doxology (which is small), and after the Doxology it is small. It begins from “Blessed is our God,” and is celebrated in the usual manner. After the litany of peace: “God is the Lord” (and not “Alleluia”). The troparia of the feast. Kathisma 1. The 1st Sessional Hymn. Kathisma 2. The 2nd Sessional Hymn. Instead of the 3rd Kathisma: the Polyeleos and Megalynarion. The 3rd Sessional Hymn. The Gradual Hymns (*Stepenny*: “From my youth”). Festal Prokimenon. Festal Gospel. (“Having seen the Resurrection of Christ” is omitted. Psalm 50 [Ps. 50]) with the stichera of the feast. After which the Priest proclaims the litany: “Save, O God, Thy people,” etc., with the exclamation: “Through the mercy and compassions.” After the litany the canon of the feast is combined with the Triodion. The Heirmos of the feast, and the Katavasia of the order. At “The Theotokos and Mother of Light,” the magnification of the feast. Upon the conclusion of the canon, the Exaposteilarion of the feast, and immediately the stichera at the Praises (*Ainoi*) of the feast. Before the Doxology the Priest proclaims: “To Thee glory is due,” etc.; after this he says: “Glory to Thee Who hast shown us the light,” and the chanter reads the Doxology. After this the Priest in the epitrachelion comes forth before the royal doors and chants aloud the litany: “Let us complete our morning [prayer],” etc. Stichera at the apos- ticha from the Lenten Triodion. After this: “It is good to give praise” (twice), etc. The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. The troparion of the feast. During this the Priest comes forth from the sanctuary and says the litany: “Have mercy on us, O God.” After this litany 3 prostrations. And immediately the First Hour begins from “Come, let us worship” (thrice). After this Psalms: 5, 89, and the 100th [Pss. 5, 89, 100]. “Glory,” and “Now and,” “Alleluia” (thrice), “Lord, have mercy” (thrice). Kathisma of the day. “Glory”: Troparion of the feast; “Now and”: “What shall we call thee?” “Order my steps,” further: “Let my mouth be filled,” etc. The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. The kontakion of the feast. “Lord, have mercy” (40 times), during which the Priest comes forth and before the royal doors proclaims aloud the prayer: “Thou Who at all times.” After this: “Lord, have mercy” (thrice), etc. “More honorable,” etc. “In the name of the Lord bless, Father.” And the Priest proclaims: “God be merciful unto us,” etc., and makes 3 prostrations. After this again the Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. “Lord, have mercy” (12 times). And the Priest says the prayer: “O Christ, the true Light,” and after this the kontakion: “To thee, the champion leader,” etc. The smallest dismissal from “Glory to Thee, O Christ God,” etc.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: ется икос же чтется далее читается в царстве
units.slavonic_diplomatic: поется, ікосъ же чтется, далѣе читается: „Въ царствѣ Твоемъ егда прійдеши“. Предъ катавасіею 8-ой пѣсни поется: „Хвалимъ, благо- словимъ“ и пр., по окончаніи же катавасіи: „Богородицу и матерь свѣта“ и пр. и пѣвецъ поетъ: „Величитъ душа моя“, „Честнѣйшую“ и пр. По семъ слѣдуетъ 9-ая пѣснь 2-жды, какъ ірмосъ и какъ ката- васія.*) По скончаніи сего есть ектенія малая, и пѣвецъ читаетъ Свѣтиленъ Тройченъ гласа, и абіе стихиры на „Хвалите“-хъ. По семъ Іерей возглашаетъ: „Тебѣ слава подобаетъ“ и пр. (Молитосл.
units.english_cohort_translation: (γ) Matins with the Canon of St. Andrew of Crete. — This Matins is celebrated on Wednesday evening of the 5th week of the Holy Great Fast. It is a small Matins without the Polyeleos and without the Great Doxology. It is celebrated thus: “Blessed is our God.” “O Heavenly King,” etc., in the usual manner. After the litany of peace, instead of “God is the Lord”: “Alleluia” (thrice). The Triadica from the Lenten Triodion. Only one, and that the 8th Kathisma, and only one Sessional Hymn from the Triodion. Upon the conclusion of this, Psalm 50 [Ps. 50], and after this the Priest before the royal doors says the litany: “Save, O God,” etc., and the exclamation: “Through the mercy and compassions,” etc. (In the midst of this litany “Lord, have mercy” [thrice] is omitted.) After this the Canon of St. Andrew of Crete begins, and that in such a manner that the chanter begins to sing the Heirmos: “A helper and a protector,” etc.; upon the conclusion of this the choir sings the refrain: “Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me,” and the Priest begins to read the troparia: “Whence shall I begin to weep,” etc., the people making a bow at each. When, however, the canon of the Venerable Mary comes, he says unto the troparia the refrain: “Venerable Mary, pray unto God for us.” Unto the troparia of the Venerable Andrew: “Venerable Father Andrew, pray unto God for us.” At the 3rd ode the Katavasia is sung, and that the Heirmos of the same ode: “Establish, O Lord”; and the Sessional Hymn is read with the small litany. At the 6th ode the Katavasia: the same Heirmos of the Great Canon. After the 6th ode the small litany; the kontakion: “My soul,” is sung, and the ikos is read; further is read: “In Thy kingdom when Thou comest.” Before the Katavasia of the 8th ode is sung: “We praise, we bless, we worship,” etc.; upon the conclusion of the Katavasia: “The Theotokos and Mother of Light,” etc., and the chanter sings: “My soul doth magnify [the Lord],” “More honorable than the Cherubim,” etc. After this follows the 9th ode twice, as Heirmos and as Katavasia.[^139] Upon the conclusion of this there is the small litany, and the chanter reads the Triadicon Exaposteilarion of the tone, and immediately the stichera at the Praises (*Ainoi*). After this the Priest proclaims: “To Thee glory is due,” etc. (*Molitvoslov*, p. 142), whereunto the choir [says]: “Amen,” and further the Priest says: “Glory to Thee Who hast shown us the light.” At this the chanter reads the Doxology, during which the Priest comes forth in the epitrachelion, and upon its conclusion chants the litany: “Let us complete.” Stichera at the aposticha from the Lenten Triodion. — After this: “It is good to give praise” (twice). The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. The troparion: “Standing in the temple.” “Lord, have mercy” (40 times), “Lord, bless.” The Priest comes forth before the royal doors, proclaims: “Blessed is He Who is,” etc., and reads the prayer: “O Heavenly King.” After this: “Lord, have mercy” (thrice), “Glory,” and “Now and.” And the Priest proclaims: “Through the prayers of our holy Fathers,” etc., and makes 3 prostrations. After the prostrations the First Hour begins, which is celebrated in order without a kathisma. After the Trisagion we say the kontakion: “My soul.”

After this the Priest proclaims: “To Thee glory is due,” etc. (*Molitvoslov*, p. 142), whereunto the choir [says]: “Amen,” and further the Priest says: “Glory to Thee Who hast shown us the light.” At this the chanter reads the Doxology, during which the Priest comes forth in the epitrachelion, and upon its conclusion chants the litany: “Let us complete.” Stichera at the aposticha from the Lenten Triodion. — After this: “It is good to give praise” (twice). The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. The troparion: “Standing in the temple.” “Lord, have mercy” (40 times), “Lord, bless.” The Priest comes forth before the royal doors, proclaims: “Blessed is He Who is,” etc., and reads the prayer: “O Heavenly King.” After this: “Lord, have mercy” (thrice), “Glory,” and “Now and.” And the Priest proclaims: “Through the prayers of our holy Fathers,” etc., and makes 3 prostrations. After the prostrations the First Hour begins, which is celebrated in order without a kathisma. After the Trisagion we say the kontakion: “My soul.”

units.slavonic_diplomatic: *) Трипѣснецъ на 4-ой, 8-ой и 9-ой пѣсни только читается съ припѣвами: „Св. Апостолы молите Бога о насъ“ — и то безъ поклоновъ, но еще и ірмосы Триписнеца не поемъ и „Слава“ и „Нынѣ“ не глаголемъ.
units.english_cohort_translation: This Matins is celebrated on the Saturday of the 5th week of the Holy Great Fast. It is Matins with the Great Doxology. It is celebrated thus: The beginning is the usual one. After the litany of peace: “God is the Lord,” etc., is sung, for in the Great Fast on Saturday and on Sunday it is always taken. After “God is the Lord” the troparion: “The command secretly given” (twice); “Glory,” and “Now and,” the same. After this follows Kathisma 1 (the 16th), and the small litany, after which the kontakion: “To thee, the champion leader.” And the Priest, vested in the phelonion, opens the royal doors and before the Holy Table sings from the Akathist 3 kontakia, ending them with “Alleluia,” and 3 ikoi, ending them with: “Rejoice, Bride unwedded,” alternately. The chanter repetitively sings unto a kontakion: “Alleluia,” and unto an ikos: “Rejoice, Bride unwedded.” (It is necessary to note that during this singing we do not sit, but stand.) Upon the conclusion of the 3rd ikos follows the 2nd Kathisma (the 17th): “Blessed are the undefiled,” and immediately the small litany. After this the choir sings the kontakion: “To thee, the champion leader,” while the Priest, standing before the Holy Table, says the other 3 kontakia and ikoi. The choir answers as was stated above. Upon the conclusion of this: Psalm 50 [Ps. 50]. After this the canons: of the temple with the Heirmos on 6, and the Theotokion on 6. Katavasia: “I will open my mouth.” (If, however, the temple be dedicated to the Mother of God, then the Theotokion canon is sung on 12.) After the 3rd ode the small litany and kontakion, and again the Priest sings another 3 kontakia and 3 ikoi. At the 6th ode the canon of the temple ceases, and the canon of the Theotokos is sung with the Heirmos on 6, and in addition also the Triodion from the Triodion. Katavasia from the Triodion. After the 6th ode the small litany and the kontakion: “To thee, the champion leader,” and immediately the Priest reads the remaining 3 kontakia and ikoi from the Akathist; at the end the choir again sings: “To thee, the champion leader.” After the 8th ode: “More honorable than the Cherubim” is sung. Stichera at the Praises (*Ainoi*) from the Triodion 4. The Great Doxology. The Trisagion (thrice). The troparion of the Theotokos once. 2 litanies. The great dismissal.

units.slavonic_incipit: Євангеліи пѣвецъ чтетъ Ѱаломъ 50-ый, Іерей
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: евангелии певец чтет псалом 50 ый иерей же велегласит
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Євангеліи пѣвецъ чтетъ Ѱаломъ 50-ый, Іерей же велегласитъ екте- нію : „Спаси Боже люди твоѧ“ и пр. По сей ектеніи Трипѣснецъ изъ Тріоди. (Въ Вторникъ же Двоєпѣснецъ.) По 8-ой пѣсни не поется „Честнѣйшѹю“, но ірмосъ. (Отъ Сѹбботы Лазаревой до новыѧ Недѣли не поется „Честнѣйшѹю“, но вмѣсто того ірмосъ 9-ой пѣсни берется.) По 9-ой пѣсни Іерей выходитъ предъ царскіѧ двери на поклонъ. По 9-ой пѣсни Свѣтиленъ : „Чертогъ твой“ 3-ды. Прочаѧ порядочно. По стиховнѣхъ : „Благо есть“, и про- чаѧ обычайно съ поклонами. И начинаетсѧ Часъ I-ый. Отпѹстъ :
units.english_cohort_translation: (α) Order of Matins on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday of Passion Week. These Matins services are small with the Gospel, but without the Great Doxology. They are celebrated thus: The beginning is the usual one. After the Six Psalms the litany of peace and “Alleluia” (thrice) in the 8th Tone. Troparion: “Behold, the Bridegroom” (thrice) aloud. Then the usual kathismata and sessional hymns from the Triodion. Upon the conclusion of these the Priest, having put on the phelonion, opens the royal doors and says: “That we may be accounted worthy,” etc., “Wisdom, let us attend, let us hear the holy Gospel,” etc., as at other times, and reads the holy Gospel. After the Gospel the chanter reads Psalm 50 [Ps. 50], and the Priest chants aloud the litany: “Save, O God, Thy people,” etc. After this litany, the Triodion canon from the Triodion (and on Tuesday, the Two-Ode Canon [*Dvoopesnets*]). After the 8th ode “More honorable than the Cherubim” is not sung, but the Heirmos. (From Lazarus Saturday until New Sunday “More honorable than the Cherubim” is not sung, but instead of that the Heirmos of the 9th ode is taken.) After the 9th ode the Priest comes forth before the royal doors for a bow. After the 9th ode the Exaposteilarion: “Thy bridal chamber” (thrice). The rest in order. After the aposticha: “It is good to give praise,” and the rest in the usual manner with prostrations. And the First Hour begins. Dismissal: “The Lord, coming unto His voluntary passion.”

units.slavonic_incipit: По семъ Іерей вновь раство- ряетъ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: сем иерей внов раство ряет царския двери
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Кондакъ его. И нынѣ : весь тойже. По семъ Іерей вновь раство- ряетъ царскія двери, кадитъ и вновь глаголетъ : „О еже сподо- битися намъ“ и прочее — якъ первѣе. По евангеліи запираетъ царскія двери. Якъ по 1-омъ, такъ и по 2-омъ, 3-омъ, 4-омъ и по 5-омъ Євангеліи (суть оубо тогда 12 Євангелій) суть по три
units.english_cohort_translation: Tone 8. Troparion: “When the glorious disciples” (thrice), and after this the Priest, vested in the phelonion, immediately opens the royal doors, proclaiming: “That we may be accounted worthy.” “Wisdom, let us attend, let us hear the holy Gospel,” etc., and immediately reads the Gospel. (Kathismata and Sessional Hymns there are none.) After the Gospel: Psalm 50 [Ps. 50], and immediately the canon from the Triodion is sung. (The litany: “Save, O God,” etc., is not said.) The rest in the usual manner, as on Monday. At the end of Matins: “It is good to give praise.” Troparion: “When the glorious disciples,” etc. Litany: “Have mercy on us, O God,” etc. After the litany immediately the First Hour from “Come, let us worship,” wherein we say the troparion: “When the glorious disciples.” “Glory,” and “Now and”: Troparion of the prophecy from the Triodion: “He Who was hanged for the sake of mankind,” etc. After this: the Prokimenon, the Old Testament reading (*Paroemia*), and immediately the Prokimenon. And so: “Order my steps.” “Let my mouth be filled.” After the Trisagion: the kontakion of the Triodion: “Having taken the bread,” etc. And the dismissal.

units.slavonic_incipit: *) Сія Утреня отправляется у насъ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: сия утреня отправляется у нас в великий
units.slavonic_diplomatic: *) Сія Утреня отправляется у насъ въ Великій Четверъ вечеромъ 6-го часа.
units.english_cohort_translation: (γ) Order of Matins on Holy Great Friday.[^140] This Matins is small. It begins from: “Blessed is our God.” After this: “O Heavenly King.” The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. “Lord, have mercy” (12 times). “Come, let us worship” (thrice), etc., in the usual manner. “Glory to the holy,” etc. The Six Psalms. The litany of peace. Instead of “God is the Lord,” there is sung: “Alleluia” (thrice). Troparion: “When the glorious disciples,” and that thrice. During this the Priest enters into the holy sanctuary, and vests in the phelonion, and having opened the royal doors, censes the Holy Table, and upon the conclusion of the troparion the chanter sings: “Lord, have mercy” (twice), “To Thee, O Lord,” “Amen,” whereunto the Priest proclaims: “That we may be accounted worthy,” etc., “Peace be to all,” etc., “Wisdom, let us attend, let us hear the holy Gospel,” etc., and reads the holy Gospel at the royal doors. The choir before the Gospel says: “Glory to Thy passions, O Lord,” and after the Gospel: “Glory to Thy long-suffering, O Lord.” After the Gospel the Priest shuts the royal doors, and the chanter sings 3 antiphons from the Triodion. After the 3rd antiphon, the Sessional Hymn; “Glory”: its kontakion; “Now and”: the very same. After this the Priest opens again the royal doors, censes, and again says: “That we may be accounted worthy,” and the rest—as before. After the Gospel he shuts the royal doors. As after the 1st, so also after the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and after the 5th Gospel (there are therefore then 12 Gospels) there are three antiphons and one Sessional Hymn. After the 6th Gospel there are the Beati- tudes (*Blazhenny*), which are read, and after which the Priest from the sanctuary proclaims: “Let us attend, peace be to all, wisdom, let us attend,” and the Prokimenon is sung. After the Prokimenon: “That we may be accounted worthy,” etc., and the 7th Gospel is read. After the 7th Gospel Psalm 50 [Ps. 50], “Have mercy on me, O God,” is read, after which immediately: “That we may be accounted worthy,” and the 8th Gospel is read. (Here the censing ceases.) After the 8th Gospel: the Three-Ode Canon (*Triodion*). In the Three-Ode Canon before the 9th ode of the canon: “We praise, we bless,” etc., and the Priest proclaims: “The Theotokos and Mother of Light,” etc., whereunto “More honorable than the Cherubim” is not sung, but the Heirmos. After the 9th ode there is a litany, the Exaposteilarion. After the Exaposteilarion: “That we may be accounted worthy,” etc., and the 9th Gospel is read; and after the 9th Gospel, the stichera at the Praises (*Ainoi*). After this, the 10th Gospel. After the 10th Gospel immediately the Priest proclaims: “Glory to God Who hath shown us the light,” and the Small Doxology is read. After this the Priest comes forth in the epitrachelion before the royal doors and chants the litany: “Let us complete.” After the litany: “That we may be accounted worthy,” and the 11th Gospel is read, and the stichera at the aposticha with their refrains. After the aposticha, the 12th Gospel. After the 12th Gospel: “It is good to give praise,” etc. (twice). Further: The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. Troparion: “Thou hast redeemed us.” After this the litany: “Have mercy on us, O God,” before the royal doors. The small dismissal. The Priest: “Wisdom”; the choir: “More honorable than the Cherubim,” etc. — (The First Hour is not joined unto this Matins.)

units.slavonic_incipit: „Блаженни непорочніи“ (каѳ. 17.) съ припѣвы
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: блаженни непорочнии каф 17 с припевы на 3
units.slavonic_diplomatic: „Блаженни непорочніи“ (каѳ. 17.) съ припѣвы на 3 статіи, и то такъ, что пѣвецъ начинаетъ пѣти припѣвы*), а священникъ въ *) Припѣвы: 1-ый „Величаемъ тя жизнодавче Христе“ и пр.; 2-ый „Достойно есть“; а 3-ій „Роди вси пѣснь“ и пр.
units.english_cohort_translation: This Matins is great with stases (*statii*). The Priest in a black epitrachelion makes the usual beginning: “Blessed is our God,” “O Heavenly King,” and the rest in the usual manner. “Our Father” with the exclamation. “Lord, have mercy” (12 times), and immediately the Priest proclaims: “Glory to the holy,” etc. (From “Come, let us worship” [thrice] even unto “Glory to the holy,” the psalms, troparia, and litany found there are omitted.) After “Glory to the holy,” there is said: “Glory to God in the highest,” etc. (thrice), and “O Lord, open Thou my lips,” etc. (twice). The Six Psalms. The litany of peace. At “God is the Lord,” the troparion: “The noble Joseph”; “Glory”: “When Thou didst descend”; “Now and”: “Unto the myrrh-bearing women.” After this the small litany, and there is sung: “Blessed are the undefiled” (Kathisma 17) with refrains in 3 stases, and that in such wise that the chanter begins to sing the refrains,[^141] while the Priest, vested in the phelonion before the holy tomb, sings the troparia. The 1st and 2nd stasis is sung in Tone 5, and the 3rd in Tone 3. After the 1st and 2nd stasis there is the small litany. After the 3rd stasis there are the troparia after the Evlogitaria (*Neporochny*): “The angelic host.” The small litany and the Sessional Hymn. After this Psalm 50 [Ps. 50], and immediately the canon: “Unto Him Who of old drowned,” wherein before the 9th ode at the exclamation of the Priest: “The Theotokos and Mother of Light,” there is sung: “Weep not for Me, O Mother.” After the 9th ode, instead of the Exaposteilarion, there is sung: “Holy is the Lord our God” (thrice). Stichera at the Praises (*Ainoi*) 4. After this the Priest vests in the phelonion and in all the priestly vestments, and from the sanctuary comes forth before the royal doors onto the ambo, proclaiming: “Glory to God Who hath shown us the light.” Whereunto the Great Doxology is sung. — After the Doxology, the Trisagion. After the Trisagion: “Come, let us bless Joseph.” During which the Priest enters into the holy sanctuary, and with the Gospel makes the entrance around the Holy Table, candle-bearers going before, and coming before the royal doors, proclaims: “Wisdom, let us attend,”[^142] while the choir sings: “The noble Joseph,” and “He Who holds the ends [of the earth].” During this the Priest goes unto the high place, and there proclaims: “Let us attend, peace be to all, wisdom, let us attend,” and they sing the Prokimenon: “Arise, O Lord,” etc. The reading from the Prophecy of Ezekiel. After the Old Testament reading (*Paroemia*), the Prokimenon, and the reading from the Epistle of the holy Apostle to the Corinthians, pericope 133. After the Epistle, the Gospel according to Matthew, pericope 114. Then the litanies: “Have mercy on us, O God,” and “Let us complete,” etc. The great dismissal. (After the dismissal there takes place the kissing of the Shroud [*Plashchanytsia*], when the chanters sing the stichera in Tone 5: “Come, let us bless Joseph.”)

units.english_text: This Matins is great with stases (*statii*). The Priest in a black epitrachelion makes the usual beginning: “Blessed is our God,” “O Heavenly King,” and the rest in the usual manner. “Our Father” with the exclamation. “Lord, have mercy” (12 times), and immediately the Priest proclaims: “Glory to the holy,” etc. (From “Come, let us worship” [thrice] even unto “Glory to the holy,” the psalms, troparia, and litany found there are omitted.) After “Glory to the holy,” there is said: “Glory to God in the highest,” etc. (thrice), and “O Lord, open Thou my lips,” etc. (twice). The Six Psalms. The litany of peace. At “God is the Lord,” the troparion: “The noble Joseph”; “Glory”: “When Thou didst descend”; “Now and”: “Unto the myrrh-bearing women.” After this the small litany, and there is sung: “Blessed are the undefiled” (Kathisma 17) with refrains in 3 stases, and that in such wise that the chanter begins to sing the refrains,[^141] while the Priest, vested in the phelonion before the holy tomb, sings the troparia. The 1st and 2nd stasis is sung in Tone 5, and the 3rd in Tone 3. After the 1st and 2nd stasis there is the small litany. After the 3rd stasis there are the troparia after the Evlogitaria (*Neporochny*): “The angelic host.” The small litany and the Sessional Hymn. After this Psalm 50 [Ps. 50], and immediately the canon: “Unto Him Who of old drowned,” wherein before the 9th ode at the exclamation of the Priest: “The Theotokos and Mother of Light,” there is sung: “Weep not for Me, O Mother.” After the 9th ode, instead of the Exaposteilarion, there is sung: “Holy is the Lord our God” (thrice). Stichera at the Praises (*Ainoi*) 4. After this the Priest vests in the phelonion and in all the priestly vestments, and from the sanctuary comes forth before the royal doors onto the ambo, proclaiming: “Glory to God Who hath shown us the light.” Whereunto the Great Doxology is sung. — After the Doxology, the Trisagion. After the Trisagion: “Come, let us bless Joseph.” During which the Priest enters into the holy sanctuary, and with the Gospel makes the entrance around the Holy Table, candle-bearers going before, and coming before the royal doors, proclaims: “Wisdom, let us attend,”[^142] while the choir sings: “The noble Joseph,” and “He Who holds the ends [of the earth].” During this the Priest goes unto the high place, and there proclaims: “Let us attend, peace be to all, wisdom, let us attend,” and they sing the Prokimenon: “Arise, O Lord,” etc. The reading from the Prophecy of Ezekiel. After the Old Testament reading (*Paroemia*), the Prokimenon, and the reading from the Epistle of the holy Apostle to the Corinthians, pericope 133. After the Epistle, the Gospel according to Matthew, pericope 114. Then the litanies: “Have mercy on us, O God,” and “Let us complete,” etc. The great dismissal. (After the dismissal there takes place the kissing of the Shroud [*Plashchanytsia*], when the chanters sing the stichera in Tone 5: “Come, let us bless Joseph.”)

units.english_cohort_translation: (α) Order of Matins on the Sunday of Pascha. This Matins is without the Great Doxology, instead whereof the “Paschal Stichera” are sung. It is celebrated thus: The Priest, vested in all the priestly vestments, having taken the holy cross, opens the royal doors, and goes outside of the church, and makes a circuit of the entire church, candle-bearers going before, while singing: “Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior,” etc. After this, when all have stood before the closed church doors, the Priest, holding the cross in his hands, proclaims: “Glory to the holy,” etc. After this he sings: “Christ is risen” once, and the choir twice. After this the Priest sings the verses: “Let God arise,” and the rest, and unto each the choir sings the troparion: “Christ is risen,” in a higher voice, and repeats the words: “And unto those in the tombs bestowing life”—when he opens with the holy cross the church doors, and all enter into the church, singing: “And unto those in the tombs bestowing life.” When the Priest hath entered into the holy sanctuary, he there at the Holy Table chants the litany: “In peace let us pray to the Lord,” and there follows the Canon of St. John of Damascus on 16 (in our cathedral church on 6). After all the odes there are small litanies, when the Priest censes the Holy Table, the icons, and makes a circuit with the censer among the people, and censes the people also, greeting each person: “Christ is risen.” The exclamation is said by the Priest within the sanctuary. At the 9th ode the refrain: “The angel cried.” Exaposteilarion: “Having fallen asleep in the flesh,” etc. (thrice). After the canon they sing: “Let every breath” in Tone 1, and there follow 4 stichera at the Praises (*Ainoi*), and the Paschal Stichera: “Today a sacred Pascha,” with their refrains. When the stichera begin to be sung, the Priest comes forth with the Gospel and with the cross onto the ambo, and the people kiss the cross, the Gospel, the *Artos*, etc. These stichera conclude with: “Christ is risen” (thrice). After this the litanies: “Have mercy on us, O God,” “Let us complete,” and so the Paschal dismissal with the cross.[^143] Before the blessing the Priest, having turned unto the people, exalts the cross, saying thrice: “Christ is risen,” whereunto the people answer: “Truly He is risen,” and only after this doth he give the blessing with the cross.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: И абіе Іерей глаголетъ ектенію : „Спаси Боже“ и пр. съ возгла- *) Зри Молитвословъ стр. 478.
units.english_cohort_translation: (β) Order of Sunday Matins, if on any day in Bright Week there fall a Saint with the Polyeleos. This Matins is great, yet in such wise that instead of the Great Doxology the Paschal Stichera are sung. The Priest begins from: “Glory to the holy.” Immediately: “Christ is risen” (thrice) and with the verses: “Let God arise.” “Glory”: Troparion to the Saint; “Now and”: Theotokion. After this the litany: “In peace let us pray to the Lord.” After the litany (“God is the Lord” is not taken) the Sessional Hymns to the Saint without kathismata. The Polyeleos. The Megalynarion. The 3rd Sessional Hymn to the Saint. Gradual Hymns (*Stepenny*): “From my youth,” etc. Prokimenon to the Saint and the rest, as at other times. The Gospel to the Saint; after the Gospel: “Having seen the Resurrection of Christ,” etc. (thrice). After this (Psalm 50 [Ps. 50] is not taken) “Glory”: “Through the prayers of the Saint,” etc.; “Now and”: “Through the prayers of the Theotokos,” etc.; unto the refrain: “Have mercy on me, O God,” etc., the sticheron to the Saint. And immediately the Priest says the litany: “Save, O God,” etc., with the excla- mation. The Canon of Pascha on 8, and to the Saint on 6. The Katavasia is the Heirmos: “The Day of Resurrection,” etc. After the 3rd ode the kontakion: “Though Thou didst descend into the grave,” etc., and the ikos. After the 6th ode the kontakion and ikos to the Saint. At the 9th ode (instead of “More honorable than the Cherubim”) there is sung: “The angel cried.” After the 9th ode the Exaposteilarion: “Having fallen asleep in the flesh.” “Glory”: to the Saint; “Now and”: “Having fallen asleep in the flesh.” At the Praises (*Ainoi*) the Sunday stichera 3, to the Saint 3, and the Paschal Stichera with the refrains (instead of the Doxology), during which there takes place the kissing of the cross and of the Gospel. “Glory”: to the Saint; “Now and”: “The Day of Resurrection,” and immediately: “Christ is risen” (thrice). “Glory”: Troparion to the Saint; “Now and”: Theotokion. After this the litanies: “Have mercy on us, O God,” and “Let us complete,” and the Paschal dismissal with the cross, in which the Saint also is commemorated.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: седалными оу неделю фомин полуелей и величание праздника
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Сѣдалными. (Оу Недѣлю Ѳоминъ Полуелей и Величаніе Праздника.)
units.english_cohort_translation: Notes: (α) As regards Sunday Matins services from Thomas Sunday unto the Ascension of Christ, concerning these it must be noted that they begin from: “Glory to the holy.” — After this there is sung: “Christ is risen” (thrice). (The verses are omitted.) And immediately: “Glory to God in the highest” (thrice), etc. The usual Six Psalms. After the litany of peace the troparia at “God is the Lord.” The kathismata with the sessional hymns. (On Thomas Sunday the Polyeleos and Megalynarion of the feast.) The Gospel. “Having seen the Resurrection of Christ” (thrice), etc., in order. The prescribed canon. The Katavasia of Pascha. At the 9th ode the Priest proclaims: “The Theotokos and Mother of Light,” and the chanter sings: “The angel cried.” Stichera at the Praises (*Ainoi*), after which there is the Great Doxology, the Trisagion, etc. 2 litanies, and the Paschal dismissal with the cross.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: β) О Оутреняхъ же повседневныхъ то примѣтимъ, что сіи оутрени такъ начинаются и кончатся, какъ и недѣльныя, лишь то надо замѣтити, что по 2-ой кадизмѣ и сѣдалномъ священ- никъ выходитъ передъ царскія двери и читаетъ : „Воскресеніе
units.english_cohort_translation: (β) Concerning daily Matins services, we note that these Matins services begin and end in the same manner as the Sunday ones, only it must be noted that after the 2nd Kathisma and sessional hymn the Priest comes forth before the royal doors and reads: “Having seen the Resurrection of Christ” once. And immediately Psalm 50 [Ps. 50]. After this the appointed canon (of the day and of the Saint). The Katavasia of the order, only after the 3rd, 6th, 8th, and 9th ode. At the 9th ode there is sung: “More honorable than the Cherubim.” The stichera at the Praises (*Ainoi*) are always from the Pentecostarion (*Flowery Triodion*). The Small Doxology, after which the Priest comes forth before the royal doors and proclaims aloud the litany: “Let us complete.” Stichera at the aposticha from the Pentecostarion. After: “It is good to give praise,” the troparion of the Saint; “Glory,” and “Now and”: of the feast of Pascha. After this the Priest again comes forth before the royal doors and chants the litany: “Have mercy on us, O God.” The dismissal without the cross: “He Who rose from the dead.”

units.slavonic_incipit: Євангеліемъ (послѣ котораго есть и „Воскресеніе
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: евангелием после котораго ест и воскресение христово и
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Євангеліемъ (послѣ котораго есть и „Воскресеніе Христово“) и съ Великимъ Славословіемъ. Здѣсь лишь то потребно замѣтити, что когда пѣвцы по Великомъ Славословіи поютъ Трисвятое, Іерей въ всю священническую одежду облеченъ идетъ къ св. Трапезѣ, кадитъ тѣй выложенный крестъ, и несетъ его около св. Престола, взимая его на главѣ, предъ царскія двери предидущимъ свѣще- носцамъ, и тамо ставъ, ожидаетъ конецъ Трисвятаго. По скон- чаніи же сего возглашаетъ : „Премудрость прости“, на что ликъ поетъ тропарь : „Спаси Господи“ и пр. По семъ Іерей идетъ къ назначенному столу, и полагаетъ верхъ его честный крестъ и ка- дитъ его отъ четырёхъ странъ и поклоншеся ему возметъ въ рѣки и станетъ предъ столцемъ зря къ востоку и возглашаетъ ектенію : „Помилуй насъ Боже“ и пр., начто ликъ воспоетъ : „Го- споди помилуй“ 12. низшимъ и вызшимъ голосомъ, подъ кото- рымъ пѣніемъ Іерей пущаетъ и воздвижаетъ свят. крестъ благо- словляя имъ народъ. — По семъ отходитъ на правую страну, смотря на сѣверъ и продолжаетъ ектенію : „Еще молимся о благовѣрномъ Царѣ нашемъ“ и проч., на что ликъ вновь поетъ 12-разъ Господи помилуй, какъ первѣе, подъ которымъ Іерей вновь пущаетъ и воздвижаетъ ч. крестъ; далѣе идетъ на 3-ью страну и обращаяся къ западу продолжаетъ ектенію : „Еще молимся о боголюбивомъ Єпископѣ“ и пр., начто ликъ вновь поетъ : „Го- споди пом.“ 12-разъ высше и низже, Іерей же подъ самымъ пѣ- ніемъ ниспущаетъ и воздвизаетъ св. крестъ, и чинитъ нимъ бла- гословеніе. На конецъ идетъ на 4-ую страну, смотря на югъ и поетъ : „Еще молимся о предстоящихъ людей“ и пр., и ликъ вновь поетъ : „Господи пом.“ 12. и все бываетъ какъ первѣе. По семъ Іерей стоя передъ столомъ, поетъ возгласъ, по скончаніи ко- тораго полагаетъ ч. крестъ на тетраподѣ и поется : „Кресту твоему“ 3-ды съ поклонами. Послѣ сего же Іерей цѣлуетъ св.
units.english_cohort_translation: This Matins is great festal with the Polyeleos, with the Gospel (after which is also “Having seen the Resurrection of Christ”), and with the Great Doxology. Here it is only needful to note that when the chanters after the Great Doxology sing the Trisagion, the Priest, vested in all the priestly vestments, goes unto the Holy Table, censes the precious cross displayed there, and carries it around the Holy Table, taking it upon his head, before the royal doors, candle-bearers going before, and standing there, awaits the end of the Trisagion. Upon the conclusion thereof he proclaims: “Wisdom, let us attend,” whereunto the choir sings the troparion: “Save, O Lord, Thy people,” etc. After this the Priest goes unto the appointed table, and places upon it the precious cross, and censes it from four sides, and having bowed unto it, takes it into his hands, and stands before the table, facing the east, and proclaims the litany: “Have mercy on us, O God,” etc., whereunto the choir sings: “Lord, have mercy” (12 times) in a lower and higher voice, during which singing the Priest lowers and exalts the holy cross, blessing the people therewith. — After this he withdraws unto the right side, facing north, and continues the litany: “Again we pray for our most devout Sovereign,” etc., whereunto the choir again sings 12 times: “Lord, have mercy,” as before, during which the Priest again lowers and exalts the precious cross; further he goes unto the 3rd side, and turning unto the west, continues the litany: “Again we pray for our God-loving Bishop,” etc., whereunto the choir again sings: “Lord, have mercy” 12 times, higher and lower, while the Priest during the very singing lowers and exalts the holy cross, and makes a blessing therewith. Finally he goes unto the 4th side, facing south, and chants: “Again we pray for the people here present,” etc., and the choir again sings: “Lord, have mercy” (12 times), and all takes place as before. After this the Priest, standing before the table, chants the exclamation, upon the conclusion of which he places the precious cross upon the Tetrapod, and there is sung: “Thy Cross do we adore, O Master,” (thrice) with prostrations. After this the Priest kisses the holy cross, and withdraws unto the Holy Table, and the people during this kiss the holy cross, and the stichera of the holy cross are sung: “Come, ye faithful,” etc., until the kissing is completed. After this the Priest, standing at the Holy Table, chants the litany: “Let us complete,” etc. The great dismissal.

units.english_cohort_translation: Note: From this Matins the Matins on the “Sunday of the Adoration of the Cross” differs in the following: After the Great Doxology, when the choir sings the “Trisagion,” the Priest goes unto the Holy Ta- ble, and having censed the cross there, carries it around the Holy Table unto the royal doors, and here proclaims: “Wisdom, let us attend,” whereunto the choir immediately sings: “Save, O Lord, Thy people,” etc. During this singing the Priest places the holy cross upon the prepared table, and there is sung: “Thy Cross do we adore, O Master,” (thrice) with prostrations. Upon the conclusion of this singing the Priest, having kissed the holy cross, leaves the Tetrapod and goes unto the Holy Table, whereupon the people kiss the cross. During this time the choir sings: “Come, ye faithful,” etc. Upon the conclusion of this the Priest at the Holy Table says the litanies: “Have mercy on us, O God,” and “Let us complete,” etc. The great dismissal.

units.english_cohort_translation: The First Hour. If the First Hour is combined with Matins, then upon the conclusion of Matins the chanter immediately begins: “Come, let us worship” (thrice). If, however, it is celebrated separately without Matins, then the Priest in the epitrachelion before the royal doors proclaims aloud: “Blessed is our God.” “O Heavenly King.” The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. “Lord, have mercy” (12 times). “Come, let us worship” (thrice). (The Priest enters into the holy sanctuary.) The chanter begins to read Psalms: 5, 89, and 100 [Pss. 5, 89, 100]. “Alleluia” (thrice). “Lord, have mercy” (thrice). “Glory,” and “Now and”: Troparion of the Sunday, or of the feast, or of the Saint, if there be a great or middle Saint; if, however, there be a small Saint, then “Glory”: Troparion of the day; “Now and”: “What shall we call thee?” After this: “Order my steps.” “Let my mouth be filled.” The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. The kontakion of the Sunday, or to the Saint, or of the feast. If, however, there be a small Saint, then the kontakion of the day is taken. “Lord, have mercy” (40 times). During this the Priest comes forth and reads before the royal doors the prayer: “Thou Who at all times.” After this the chanter says: “Lord, have mercy” (thrice), “Glory,” and “Now and”: “More honorable than the Cherubim,” etc., and “In the name of the Lord bless, Father”; whereunto the Priest proclaims: “God be bountiful unto us,” etc., and reads the prayer: “O Christ, the true Light,” etc. After this prayer there immediately begins:

units.slavonic_incipit: Отче нашъ съ возгласомъ. Кондакъ храму,
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: отче наш с возгласом кондак храму дню и
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Отче нашъ съ возгласомъ. Кондакъ храму, дню и Святому. Го- споди пом. 40. Слава и Нынѣ. Честнѣйшую. „Именемъ Господ- нимъ благослови Отче“, на что Іерей вшедше въ епитрахилѣ пе- редъ царскія двери, глаголетъ : „Молитвами св. Отецъ“ и пр. и чтетъ молитву : „Всесвятая Тройце“. По семъ пѣвецъ поетъ :
units.english_cohort_translation: The Typika [*Obidnytsia*] is celebrated then if there will be no Liturgy, and it is celebrated thus: The Priest having given the blessing, the chanter makes the usual beginning and reads the Psalms with the refrain: “Bless the Lord, O my soul,[^147] blessed art Thou, O Lord.” “Glory”: “Praise the Lord, O my soul”; “Now and”: “Only-begotten Son” (is sung). The Beatitudes (*Blazhenny*). Stichera at the Beatitudes from the Octoechos according to the 8 tones. After this the Priest, having put on the phelonion, opens the royal doors and proclaims: “Let us attend, peace be to all, wisdom, let us attend,” and the chanter sings the Prokimenon of the day. After this follows: the Epistle (*Apostol*). During the reading of the Epistle the Priest censes the sanctuary, and after it says: “Peace be to thee, wisdom, let us attend,” and immediately: “Wisdom, let us attend,” etc., and reads the holy Gospel. After the Gospel he shuts the royal doors. After this the choir sings: “Remember us, O Lord.” “The heavenly choir.” The Creed (*Viruyu*). “Pardon, remit.” “Our Father” with the exclamation. The kontakion of the temple, of the day, and to the Saint. “Lord, have mercy” (40 times). “Glory,” and “Now and”: “More honorable than the Cherubim.” “In the name of the Lord bless, Father”; whereunto the Priest, having come in the epitrachelion before the royal doors, says: “Through the prayers of our holy Fathers,” etc., and reads the prayer: “All-Holy Trinity.” After this the chanter sings: “Blessed be the name of the Lord” (thrice). “I will bless the Lord.” “It is meet and right... unto “the Mother of our God.” After this: “Wisdom.” “More honorable than the Cherubim,” etc. The small dismissal.
units.slavonic_text: Отче нашъ съ возгласомъ. Кондакъ храму, дню и Святому. Го- споди пом. 40. Слава и Нынѣ. Честнѣйшую. „Именемъ Господ- нимъ благослови Отче“, на что Іерей вшедше въ епитрахилѣ пе- редъ царскія двери, глаголетъ : „Молитвами св. Отецъ“ и пр. и чтетъ молитву : „Всесвятая Тройце“. По семъ пѣвецъ поетъ :
units.english_text: The Typika [*Obidnytsia*] is celebrated then if there will be no Liturgy, and it is celebrated thus: The Priest having given the blessing, the chanter makes the usual beginning and reads the Psalms with the refrain: “Bless the Lord, O my soul,[^147] blessed art Thou, O Lord.” “Glory”: “Praise the Lord, O my soul”; “Now and”: “Only-begotten Son” (is sung). The Beatitudes (*Blazhenny*). Stichera at the Beatitudes from the Octoechos according to the 8 tones. After this the Priest, having put on the phelonion, opens the royal doors and proclaims: “Let us attend, peace be to all, wisdom, let us attend,” and the chanter sings the Prokimenon of the day. After this follows: the Epistle (*Apostol*). During the reading of the Epistle the Priest censes the sanctuary, and after it says: “Peace be to thee, wisdom, let us attend,” and immediately: “Wisdom, let us attend,” etc., and reads the holy Gospel. After the Gospel he shuts the royal doors. After this the choir sings: “Remember us, O Lord.” “The heavenly choir.” The Creed (*Viruyu*). “Pardon, remit.” “Our Father” with the exclamation. The kontakion of the temple, of the day, and to the Saint. “Lord, have mercy” (40 times). “Glory,” and “Now and”: “More honorable than the Cherubim.” “In the name of the Lord bless, Father”; whereunto the Priest, having come in the epitrachelion before the royal doors, says: “Through the prayers of our holy Fathers,” etc., and reads the prayer: “All-Holy Trinity.” After this the chanter sings: “Blessed be the name of the Lord” (thrice). “I will bless the Lord.” “It is meet and right... unto “the Mother of our God.” After this: “Wisdom.” “More honorable than the Cherubim,” etc. The small dismissal.

units.english_cohort_translation: They are celebrated in the same manner as the ordinary Hours. — Here it is only needful to note that at all the Hours, instead of the usual psalms, other psalms are prescribed. Besides this, after the troparia 3 stichera are sung with “Glory,” and “Now and.” After this the Priest from the sanctuary says: “Let us attend, peace be to all, wisdom, let us attend.” Whereunto the chanter sings the Prokimenon. After this there is one reading from the Old and one from the New Testament. After the readings the Priest opens the royal doors, proclaiming: “Wisdom, let us attend,” etc., and at the royal doors reads the Gospel. After the Gospel he shuts the royal doors. The chanter reads: “Order my steps” at the 1st, “Blessed is the Lord God” at the 3rd, “Let Thy compassions quickly go before us” at the 6th, and “Deliver us not up” at the 9th Hour. All the rest are concluded in order, as at the simple Hours, that is, when “Lord, have mercy” is said 40 times, the Priest comes forth before the royal doors in the epitrachelion, and there says all things as at other times. After the prayer of the Ninth Hour there are also taken from the Typika [*Obidnytsia*] certain parts for completion, and that: (α) On the Eve of the Nativity and of Theophany: “Bless the Lord, O my soul.” “Glory”: “Praise the Lord, O my soul.” “Now and”: “Only-begotten Son.” After this: “In Thy kingdom.” “Glory,” and “Now and”: “Remember us.” “The heavenly choir.” The Creed (*Viruyu*). “Pardon, remit.” “Our Father.” The kontakion of the feast. “Lord, have mercy” (40 times), and “Through the prayers of our holy Fathers,” etc., when the Priest comes forth before the royal doors, and there reads the prayer: “All-Holy Trinity.” After this: “Blessed be the name of the Lord” (thrice). “I will bless the Lord at all times.” “It is meet and right,” and the dismissal. (If, however, there is a Liturgy, then after the prayer: “All-Holy Trinity,” there is immediately the dismissal. “Blessed be the name of the Lord” [thrice] and “I will bless the Lord at all times” are taken at the end of the Liturgy.)

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Нынѣ. Аллилуя 3. Господи пом. 3. Кадизма дню.**) Вмѣсто тро- паря глаголется : „За оутра оуслыши“. Слава и Нынѣ : „Что тя наречемъ“. „Стопы моя“***) „Да исполнятся“. Трисвятое. Отче нашъ съ возгласомъ. Вмѣсто кондака берется : „Скоро предвари“.
units.english_cohort_translation: The First Hour is celebrated for the most part with Matins, and begins only from: “Come, let us worship” (thrice). (The Priest enters into the sanctuary.)[^148] The chanter reads the three appointed Psalms. “Glory,” and “Now and.” “Alleluia” (thrice). “Lord, have mercy” (thrice). Kathisma of the day.[^149] Instead of the troparion there is said: “In the morning hear my voice, O my King and my God.” “Glory,” and “Now and”: “What shall we call thee, O full of grace?” “Order my steps”[^150] “Let my mouth be filled.” The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. Instead of the kontakion there is taken: “Let Thy compassions quickly go before us.” “Glory”: “Wisdom.” “Now and”: “All-holy [Theotokos].” “Lord, have mercy” (40 times). And the Priest, having come forth from the sanctuary, says the prayer: “Thou Who at all times.” After this the chanter says: “Lord, have mercy” (thrice), “Glory,” and “Now and”: “More honorable than the Cherubim,” etc., “In the name of the Lord,” etc., and the Priest proclaims: “God be bountiful unto us, and bless us, and show the light of His countenance upon us, and have mercy on us,” and makes 3 prostrations. After this the chanter: The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. “Lord, have mercy” (12 times). Whereunto the Priest says the prayer: “O Christ, the true Light.” Upon the conclusion of which the chanter sings the kontakion of the Annunciation: “To thee, the champion leader,” etc., and if this Hour is combined with Matins, he makes the smallest dismissal.

units.slavonic_incipit: На что Іерей глаголетъ молитву :
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: на что иерей глаголет молитву христе свете
units.slavonic_diplomatic: На что Іерей глаголетъ молитву : „Христе свѣте истинный“. По скончаніи которой пѣвецъ поетъ кондакъ Благовѣщенія : „Взб- ранной воеводѣ“ и пр. и если сей часъ съ Оутренею есть соко- вѣпленъ, то чинитъ отпустъ найменьшій.
units.english_cohort_translation: The Third Hour, if it is celebrated together with the 1st Hour, begins from: “Come, let us worship” (thrice), when the Priest departs from the royal doors. If, however, it is celebrated separately, then from: “Blessed is our God.” “O Heavenly King.” “Our Father,” etc. After this, following “Come, let us worship” (thrice), the appointed Psalms. “Glory,” and “Now and.” “Alleluia” (thrice). “Lord, have mercy” (thrice). Kathisma of the day. After the kathisma the troparion of the Fast: “O Lord, Who at the third hour didst send down Thy Most Holy Spirit upon Thine Apostles, take Him not away from us, O Good One, but renew Him in us who pray unto Thee.” “Glory,” and “Now and”: “O Theotokos, thou art the true vine”; and there is read: “Blessed is the Lord God,” etc. After this: The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. Instead of the kontakion there is sung the troparion of the Fast: “Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God,” with “Glory,” and “Now and.” “Lord, have mercy” (40 times). And the Priest, having come forth from the sanctuary before the royal doors, says the prayer: “Thou Who at all times.” After this the chanter: “Glory,” and “Now and”: “More honorable than the Cherubim,” etc., “In the name of the Lord bless, Father,” and the Priest proclaims: “Through the prayers of our holy Fathers,” etc., and makes 3 prostrations. After this: The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. “Lord, have mercy” (12 times), and the Priest reads the prayer: “O Master God,” etc., and immediately:

units.slavonic_incipit: „Скоро да предваритъ“ читается. По семъ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: скоро да предварит читается по сем трисвятое
units.slavonic_diplomatic: „Скоро да предваритъ“ читается. По семъ : Трисвятое. Отче нашъ съ возгласомъ. Вмѣсто кондака тропарь поста : „Спасеніе содѣлалъ“ съ Слава и Нынѣ. Господи пом. 40., когда Іерей вы- ходитъ изъ олтаря и читаетъ молитву : „Иже на всякое время“.
units.english_cohort_translation: The Sixth Hour from “Come, let us worship” (thrice), when the Priest enters into the holy sanctuary. The chanter reads the three psalms. “Glory,” and “Now and.” “Alleluia” (thrice). “Lord, have mercy” (thrice). Kathisma of the day. Troparion of the Fast: “Thou Who on the sixth day and hour didst nail to the Cross the sin which Adam daringly committed in paradise,” etc. “Glory,” and “Now and”: “Seeing that we have not boldness,” etc. “Let Thy compassions quickly go before us” is read. After this: The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. Instead of the kontakion the troparion of the Fast: “Thou hast wrought salvation,” with “Glory,” and “Now and.” “Lord, have mercy” (40 times), when the Priest comes forth from the sanctuary and reads the prayer: “Thou Who at all times.” “Glory,” and “Now and.” “More honorable than the Cherubim,” etc., “In the name of the Lord bless, Father,” whereunto the Priest proclaims: “Through the prayers of our holy Fathers,” etc., and makes 3 prostrations. After this: The Trisagion. “Our Father” with the exclamation. “Lord, have mercy” (12 times), and the prayer is said by the Priest: “O God and Lord of hosts,” and so forth.

units.slavonic_incipit: Литіею и изъ Оутрени съ І-ымъ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: литиею и из оутрени с и ым часом мы
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Литіею и изъ Оутрени съ І-ымъ Часомъ. Мы чинъ сего богослу- женія тѣй еще разъ не намѣряемъ описати, единокаждый бо знати будетъ его оужъ изъ сказанныхъ. Тѣй лишь то примѣ- тимъ, что если Всенощное бдѣніе такъ зачинается, что Іерей раз- творивъ царскія двери и покадивъ церковь, оу царскихъ дверей на „Повелите“ возглашаетъ : „Слава святѣй“ и такъ Прійдите покл.
units.english_cohort_translation: The All-Night Vigil consists of Great Vespers with Litiya and of Matins with the 1st Hour,—or of Great Compline with Litiya and of Matins with the 1st Hour. We do not intend to describe the order of this divine service here yet again, for each one will already know it from the things spoken. Here let us only note this: that if the All-Night Vigil begins in such wise that the Priest, having opened the royal doors and censed the church, at the royal doors at “Command” [*Povelite*] proclaims: “Glory to the Holy,” and thus “Come, let us worship” (thrice); then at the beginning of Matins let him not proclaim anew “Glory to the Holy,” but instead of this let him say: “Blessed and glorified is Christ our God,” and thus let there follow: “Glory to God in the highest” (twice). If, however, at the beginning of Matins there is to be said: “Glory to the Holy,” then at the end of the Litiya let there be said: “The blessing of the Lord be upon you.”

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: в западно латинской церкви ест закон по кото
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Въ западно-латинской церкви есть законъ (lex), по кото- ромъ не токмо Іерей, но еще и поддіаконъ ежедневно (quotidie) подъ тяжкимъ грѣхомъ (sub peccato mortali) обязантъ есть Пра- вило Церковное (Breviarium) отправляти. Кромѣ сего тѣ лица же церковныя, которыя еще и нѣкую церковную бенефицію имѣютъ, не токмо грѣшатъ, если Правило Церковное не откончатъ, но еще и обязанны суть въ совѣсти припадающую часть доходовъ сво- ихъ на побожныя цѣли дати, т. е. они не токмо подъ тяжкимъ грѣхомъ, но еще и съ обязанностію возданія (sub onere resti- tutionis) должны отправляти Церковное Правило.
units.english_cohort_translation: In the Western Latin Church there is a law (*lex* [law]), according to which not only a Priest, but also a subdeacon daily (*quotidie* [daily]) under mortal sin (*sub peccato mortali* [under mortal sin]) is bound to celebrate the Church Rule (*Breviarium* [Breviary]). Moreover, those ecclesiastical persons who also hold some ecclesiastical benefice not only sin if they do not complete the Church Rule, but also are bound in conscience to give the corresponding portion of their revenues unto pious purposes, that is, they are bound to celebrate the Church Rule not only under mortal sin, but also under obligation of restitution (*sub onere restitutionis* [under obligation of restitution]).

units.slavonic_incipit: IX. Пій Папа двѣмъ священникамъ такъ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: пий папа двем священникам так отвечал
units.slavonic_diplomatic: IX. Пій Папа двѣмъ священникамъ такъ отвѣчалъ : „Sequantur praxim aliorum piorum Sacerdotum illius regionis.“ (Cfr. Zeitschrift für Kath. Theolog. VII. Jahrgang. I. Heft. 1883. S. 188.)
units.english_cohort_translation: In the Eastern Greek Church, however, there is no such clear definition. There are those who, according to the words of the Constitution of Benedict XIV *“Eo quamvis,”* say this: that among us the obligation to fulfill the Church Rule hath arisen not by express law (*nulla lege expressa* [by no express law]), but by praiseworthy custom (*laudabili consuetudine* [by praiseworthy custom]). Yet among us it is not even known whether a presbyter, or already also a subdeacon, is bound unto this. Further, neither is it known when a priest is bound unto this: whether daily (*quotidie* [daily]), or only when he celebrates the Liturgy? It seems to me that it is a praiseworthy matter to celebrate the Rule daily (*quotidie* [daily]); but it appears that it is prescribed under mortal sin (*sub peccato mortali* [under mortal sin]) only when the Priest celebrates the Holy Liturgy. For so it is found in the Oriental Code, law 66a (*in Codice Orientali lege 66-a*): *“Sacerdos non recitans horas canonicas et celebrat, peccat; si suppleverit, remittitur peccatum”* [“A priest who doth not recite the canonical hours and celebrates, sins; if he shall have supplied them, the sin is remitted”] (Papp-Szilágyi: *Enchiridion juris Eccl. Orient.*, Magno-Varadini, 1862, p. 77). Likewise it is not known whether a priest who hath a church parish is obliged, if he doth not complete the Church Rule, to give the due portion from his revenues unto pious purposes, that is, whether he is bound to fulfill the rule under obligation of restitution (*sub onere restitutionis* [under obligation of restitution]), or not? Finally, since among us the Church Rule is lengthy and requires many books for its conscientious completion, and in many places books are not even to be had: therefore it is not known how many of the services a priest ought to complete. A full rule, or an abbreviated one? Unto this question Pope Pius IX answered two priests thus: *“Sequantur praxim aliorum piorum Sacerdotum illius regionis”* [“Let them follow the practice of other pious priests of that region”] (cf. *Zeitschrift für Kath. Theolog.*, VII. Jahrgang, I. Heft, 1883, p. 188).

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: трапезе и после пения его поет ектению
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Трапезѣ и послѣ пѣнія его поетъ ектенію : „Рцемъ вси“. По семъ пѣвецъ читаетъ : „Сподоби Господи“, по скончаніи котораго Іерей поетъ вторую ектенію : „Исполнимъ“. Стихиры на стиховнѣхъ 4, и то воскресныя изъ Октоиха. (Святому ничего не беремъ.) Сла- ва : Святому. И нынѣ : Богородиченъ воскресенъ отъ стиховныхъ по гласу Святаго. Если же Святому стихиры писанной на Слава нѣсть, тогда Слава и Нынѣ : Богородиченъ изъ стиховнѣхъ. По „Нынѣ отпущаеши“ тропарь воскресенъ. Слава : Святому, И нынѣ :
units.english_cohort_translation: (α) On Saturday at Great Vespers: The usual beginning, the litany of peace. Kathisma: “Blessed is the man,” entire. Stichera on “Lord, I have cried” at 10, and that: 7 of the Resurrection from the Octoechos, and to the Saint 3 from the Anthologion or from the Common Menaion [*Obshchina*]. “Glory”: to the Saint, if he have one; if, however, he have none: “Glory,” and “Now and”: The Dogmatikon of the current tone from the Octoechos. Great entrance. “O Joyful Light.” Great Prokimenon (“The Lord reigns”). During the Prokimenon the Priest comes unto the Holy Table, and after its singing sings the litany: “Let us all say.” After this the chanter reads: “Vouchsafe, O Lord,” upon the conclusion of which the Priest sings the second litany: “Let us complete.” Stichera on the aposticha 4, and those of the Resurrection from the Octoechos. (Unto the Saint we take nothing.) “Glory”: to the Saint. “Now and”: Theotokion of the Resurrection from the aposticha according to the tone of the Saint. If, however, there is no sticheron written for the Saint at “Glory,” then “Glory,” and “Now and”: Theotokion from the aposticha. After “Now lettest Thou dismiss” the troparion of the Resurrection. “Glory”: to the Saint. “Now and”: Theotokion of the Resurrection from the troparia of the Resurrection according to the tone of the troparion of the Saint. Great dismissal.

units.slavonic_incipit: „Воскресеніе Христово“. Ѱаломъ 50. съ стихирами.
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: воскресение христово псалом 50 с стихирами канон 4 го
units.slavonic_diplomatic: „Воскресеніе Христово“. Ѱаломъ 50. съ стихирами. Канонъ 4-го- бый и берется на 14. (Воскресенъ съ ірмосомъ на 4, Крестовоскре- сенъ на 3, Богородиченъ на 3, а Святому на 4.) Катавасіа ря- довая. По 3-ой пѣсни канона и ектеніи : кондакъ и ікосъ Свя- таго. Слава : Сѣдаленъ Святаго. И нынѣ : Богородиченъ. По 6-ой пѣсни : кондакъ и ікосъ воскресенъ. На 8-ою пѣснь : „Величитъ душа моя“. Честнѣйшую и пр. По 9-ой пѣсни : ектенія малая, послѣ которой Іерей возглашаетъ :*) „Святъ Господь Богъ нашъ“, пѣвецъ тоже 2-жды и Свѣтиленъ воскресенъ. Слава : Свѣтиленъ
units.english_cohort_translation: [*Stepenny*]. During this the Priest comes vested in the phelonion unto the Holy Table, and there proclaims: “Let us attend, peace be to all, wisdom, let us attend,” and the chanter sings the Prokimenon. At “Let us pray to the Lord” the Priest opens the royal doors—and the rest as usual. The Gospel. “Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ.” Psalm 50 [Ps. 50] with the stichera. The Canon is fourfold and is taken at 14 (of the Resurrection with the heirmos at 4, of the Cross and Resurrection at 3, of the Theotokos at 3, and to the Saint at 4). Katavasia of the day. After Ode 3 of the Canon and the litany: Kontakion and ikos of the Saint. “Glory”: Sessional Hymn of the Saint. “Now and”: Theotokion. After Ode 6: Kontakion and ikos of the Resurrection. At Ode 8: “My soul doth magnify.” “More honorable than the Cherubim,” etc. After Ode 9: The small litany, after which the Priest proclaims:[^154] “Holy is the Lord our God”; the chanter the same (twice), and the Exapostilarion of the Resurrection. “Glory”: Exapostilarion of the Saint. “Now and”: Theotokion of the Resurrection. “Let every breath” and the stichera on the Praises 8 from the Octoechos. (Unto the Saint nothing is taken.) “Glory”: Gospel sticheron of the day. “Now and”: “Most blessed art thou.” Great Doxology. The Trisagion. Troparion of the Resurrection: “Today salvation is come unto the world,” or “Having risen from the tomb.” The litanies: “Have mercy on us, O God,” and “Let us complete.” Great dismissal.

units.slavonic_incipit: α) На Великой Вечерни : Начало
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: на великой вечерни начало обычайное стихиры
units.slavonic_diplomatic: α) На Великой Вечерни : Начало обычайное. Стихиры на „Го- споди воззвахъ на 10, и то : воскресныя 3, восточная 1, а Свя- томъ 6. Слава : Святомъ. И нынѣ : Богородиченъ догматъ гласа (т. е. Богородиченъ а.) Входъ великій съ кадиломъ. Прокименъ великій дню. Чтенія 3 Святомъ и пр. Стихиры на стиховнахъ всѣ воскресныя изъ Октоиха. Слава : Святомъ. И нынѣ : Богоро- диченъ по гласу тогоже „Наславник“-а. „Нынѣ отпущаеши“ и пр.
units.english_cohort_translation: (α) At Great Vespers: The usual beginning. Stichera on “Lord, I have cried” at 10, and that: 3 of the Resurrection, 1 of the East, and to the Saint 6. “Glory”: to the Saint. “Now and”: Dogmatikon Theotokion of the tone (that is, the 1st Theotokion). Great entrance with the censer. Great Prokimenon of the day. Readings 3 to the Saint, etc. Stichera on the aposticha all of the Resurrection from the Octoechos. “Glory”: to the Saint. “Now and”: Theotokion according to the tone of the same Doxastikon [*Naslavnyk*]. “Now lettest Thou dismiss,” etc. Troparion of the Resurrection. “Glory”: Troparion to the Saint. “Now and”: Theotokion of the Resurrection according to the tone. All the rest in order;

units.slavonic_incipit: Прокименъ воскресенъ. Євангеліе воскресное. „Воскресеніе Христово“.
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: прокимен воскресен евангелие воскресное воскресение христово псалом 50
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Богородиченъ тамже. Степенна. Прокименъ воскресенъ. Євангеліе воскресное. „Воскресеніе Христово“. Ѱаломъ 50. и стихира воскре- сна. Канонъ на 14, и то : воскресенъ на 4 съ ірмосомъ, кресто- воскресенъ не беремъ. Богородиченъ на 2, а Святомъ на 8. Ката- васіа рядовая. По 3-ой пѣсни кондакъ и ікосъ Святаго. Слава :
units.english_cohort_translation: (γ) At Matins: The usual beginning. At “God is the Lord” the troparion of the Resurrection (twice). “Glory”: Troparion of the Saint. “Now and”: Theotokion of the Resurrection according to the tone of the troparion of the Saint. Kathismata 2 with two Sunday Sessional Hymns and with their Theotokia. Instead of the 3rd Kathisma: The Polyeleos and the Magnification of the Saint with the selected verses. After the Magnification we do not sing “Glory,” and “Now and,” and “Alleluia,” but we sing immediately: the troparia after the Evlogitaria: “The angelic assembly.” The small litany. Sunday Hypakoe of the tone, and thus both Sessional Hymns to the Saint, once each, without Theotokia. “Glory”: Sessional Hymn of the Saint. “Now and”: Theotokion in the same place. Graduals [*Stepenny*]. Sunday Prokimenon. Gospel of the Resurrection. “Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ.” Psalm 50 [Ps. 50] and the Sunday sticheron. The Canon at 14, and that: of the Resurrection at 4 with the heirmos; of the Cross and Resurrection we do not take; of the Theotokos at 2, and to the Saint at 8. Katavasia of the day. After Ode 3: Kontakion and ikos of the Saint. “Glory”: Sessional Hymn of the Saint. “Now and”: Theotokion of the same. After Ode 6: Kontakion and ikos of the Resurrection. Before Ode 9: “My soul doth magnify” and “More honorable than the Cherubim.” After Ode 9: Small litany, and “Holy is the Lord our God,” and the Sunday Exapostilarion. After this “Glory”: to the Saint. “Now and”: Theotokion of the Resurrection. Stichera on the Praises 4 of the Resurrection, and 4 to the Saint with the Doxastikon [*Naslavnyk*] and with its two refrains, which are written on the aposticha of Vespers. “Glory”: Gospel sticheron. “Now and”: “Most blessed art thou.” Great Doxology. The Trisagion. Troparion of the Resurrection, only one of the two. All the rest as usual;

units.english_cohort_translation: (δ) At the Hours: At the 1st Hour: Troparion of the Resurrection and troparion of the Saint; after the “Our Father”: Kontakion of the Resurrection. (In the dismissals the Saint is commemorated everywhere.)

units.slavonic_diplomatic: воскресенъ съ ірмосомъ на 4, Крестовоскресенъ оставляется, Бого- родиченъ на 2, І-му Святому на 4, а ІІ-омъ Святомъ на 4. Ката- васіа рядовая. По 3-ой пѣсни кондакъ и ікосъ І-го и ІІ-го Свя- таго, сѣдаленъ І-го Святаго ; Слава : сѣдаленъ ІІ-го Святаго, И нынѣ : Богородиченъ. По 6-ой пѣсни кондакъ и ікосъ воскресенъ.
units.english_cohort_translation: (γ) At Matins: The usual beginning. At “God is the Lord” the troparion of the Resurrection and the troparion of the 1st Saint. “Glory”: Troparion of the 2nd Saint; “Now and”: Theotokion of the Resurrection according to the tone of the troparion of the 2nd Saint. All the rest of the Resurrection from the Octoechos. The Canon at 14; and that: of the Resurrection with the heirmos at 4, of the Cross and Resurrection is omitted, of the Theotokos at 2, to the 1st Saint at 4, and to the 2nd Saint at 4. Katavasia of the day. After Ode 3: Kontakion and ikos of the 1st and 2nd Saints, Sessional Hymn of the 1st Saint; “Glory”: Sessional Hymn of the 2nd Saint; “Now and”: Theotokion. After Ode 6: Kontakion and ikos of the Resurrection. After Ode 9: Exapostilarion of the 2nd Saint; “Now and”: Theotokion from the Sunday Exapostilarion; on the Praises stichera at 8, and all of the Resurrection. (Unto the Saints nothing.) “Glory”: Gospel sticheron; “Now and”: “Most blessed art thou.” After the Great Doxology and the Trisagion the troparion of the Resurrection: “Today salvation [is come unto the world],” or “Having risen from the tomb.” The rest in order;

units.english_cohort_translation: (δ) At the Hours and at the Typika [*Obidnytsia*]: All things in order, that is: at the 1st Hour: Troparion of the Resurrection; after the “Our Father,” kontakion of the Resurrection; at the 3rd Hour: Troparion of the Resurrection and troparion of the 1st Saint; after the “Our Father”: Kontakion of the 1st Saint; at the 6th Hour: Troparion of the Resurrection and troparion of the temple; after the “Our Father”: Kontakion of the temple; at the 9th Hour: Troparion of the Resurrection and troparion of the 2nd Saint; after the “Our Father”: Kontakion of the 2nd Saint. — At the Typika [*Obidnytsia*]: Kontakion of the Resurrection and of the temple. “Glory”: Troparion of the 1st Saint; “Now and”: of the 2nd Saint. All the rest in order. In the dismissals the Saints are commemorated everywhere.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: β) на Повечеріи же берется малый Святый на Вечерни оставленный, и то такъ, что съ канономъ Недѣльнымъ совокупляется и канонъ Святаго. Въ единокаждой пѣсни — сирѣчь — берется ірмосъ канона недѣльнаго и читаются тропари его съ припѣвомъ ихъ до „Слава“. Предъ „Слава“ читаются тропари изъ І-ой пѣсни канона малаго Святаго съ припѣвомъ его, но безъ „Слава“. По семъ : Слава и Нынѣ тропарь изъ канона недѣльнаго. По скончаніи І-ой пѣсни поется ірмосъ ІІ-ой пѣсни канона недѣльнаго съ тропарями его и съ тропарями малаго Святаго. Слава и Нынѣ : тропарь изъ канона недѣльнаго. — И такъ берутся всѣ пѣсни. По скончаніи же канона вмѣсто стихиръ воскресныхъ поются стихиры малаго Святаго на Вечерни оставленныя ;
units.english_cohort_translation: (β) At Compline, however, the small Saint omitted at Vespers is taken, and that in such wise that with the Sunday canon the canon of the Saint is also combined. In each ode—that is—the heirmos of the Sunday canon is taken and its troparia are read with their refrain unto “Glory.” Before “Glory” the troparia from Ode 1 of the canon of the small Saint are read with its refrain, but without “Glory.” After this: “Glory,” and “Now and,” the troparion from the Sunday canon. At the conclusion of Ode 1 the heirmos of Ode 2 [Ode 3] of the Sunday canon is sung with its troparia and with the troparia of the small Saint. “Glory,” and “Now and”: Troparion from the Sunday canon. — And thus all the odes are taken. At the conclusion of the canon, instead of the stichera of the Resurrection, the stichera of the small Saint omitted at Vespers are sung;

units.slavonic_diplomatic: δ) на Часахъ. На І-омъ Часѣ : тропарь воскресный и великаго Святаго. По „Отче нашъ“-ѣ кондакъ воскресный ; на ІІІ-омъ : тропарь воскресный и тропарь вел. Святаго. Слава : тропарь малаго Святаго. И нынѣ : Богородиченъ Часовъ. По „Отче нашъ“-ѣ кондакъ великаго Святаго ; на VI-омъ Часѣ : тропарь воскресный и тропарь храма, по „Отче нашъ“-ѣ кондакъ храма ; на ІХ-омъ Часѣ : тропарь воскресный и тропарь великаго Святаго ; по „Отче нашъ“-ѣ кондакъ малаго Святаго. Прочая обычайно.

All the rest as usual.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: в сем случае то потребно заметити что те
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Въ семъ случаѣ то потребно замѣтити, что тѣ маліи Святіи : либо : α) вкупно имѣютъ отправу, и тогда все такъ будетъ отправлятися, какъ одному Святому, имѣющему стихиры на 3, а канонъ на 4 ; либо ; β) единокаждый Святый имѣетъ свою собственную отправу, и тогда лишь отправа І-го Святаго берется, прочіи Святіи же оставляются и только въ Отпустѣ споминаются.
units.english_cohort_translation: In this case it is needful to note that those small Saints: either: (α) have their office together, and then all things will be celebrated just as for one Saint having stichera at 3 and a canon at 4; or: (β) each Saint hath his own proper office, and then only the office of the 1st Saint is taken, while the other Saints are omitted and commemorated only in the Dismissal.
